title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
cleaned_text: an unknown threat actor has infected 953 online stores most of them running magento as part of long running campaign active since july 2025 according to dutch commerce security company sansec the activity is designed to add small piece of code to the store pages that when visited by unsuspecting users serves malicious javascript loader code through magento cms blocks when you visit that code makes your browser ask the group server what to do next sansec said the server first checks whether you are real shopper or security scanner so scanners get nothing no less than five distinct domains have been observed over time in connection with the campaign manulfie click first seen in july 2025 neswnsssn click first seen in december 2025 lanhd6549tdhse top first seen in march 2026 additionalver com first seen in june 2026 deepveindrilling com first seen in october 2026 sansec said it found deepveindrilling com in the cms blocks of 83 online stores since the domain was registered on october 2026 the latest javascript loader domain is hosted behind cloudflare and only responds to script requests from real visitors of infected stores the loader is staged within magento cms block database table which is used to render static content into storefront pages the ultimate objective of the attack is to launch the attack controlled code when the cms block is rendered after shopper opens the compromised website while sansec does not disclose whether the threat actor modifies an existing cms block such as header footer or promotional banner or creates new block the attacker can adopt either of the approaches to run the loader two different versions of the loader have been spotted in one version the external javascript loaded from the attacker domain stores the payload in the browser localstorage this causes the stashed code to be run again on subsequent visits even if the external domain becomes unavailable the second version expands on this behavior by incorporating browser fingerprinting checks to filter out bots and security scanners while ensuring that only real shoppers are exposed to the malicious code the exact nature of the final payload remains unknown early iterations of the campaign have also been observed using keitaro an advertising tracker and analytics platform as traffic distribution system tds to route visitors to different responses return payload redirect or nothing based on their characteristics sansec said requesting the additionalver com script as windows desktop visitor returned as response qwe 123 which does nothing apart from setting cookie that marks the visitor for 24 hours the deepveindrilling com domain on the other hand drops the keitaro component and integrates the bot filtering logic into the loader itself as for the initial access vector 471 magento stores are estimated to have been injected with the loader through the polyshell aka cve 2026 48356 vulnerability another 102 stores saw files uploaded through the polyshell or sessionreaper aka cve 2025 54236 vulnerabilities one store on magento p1 had polyshell webshells disguised as png images in pub media custom options quote next to the additionalver com loader in cms block sansec said the block switched to deepveindrilling com on october the store still lacks apsb26 73 adobe polyshell fix for supported release lines in another case an commerce store running magento p10 with no missing core patches was compromised to add rogue administrator account and then use it to inject the code site owners are advised to audit their sites for suspicious accounts and unexpected cms blocks in the cms block and cms page tables it also advised to keep the sites up to date and enforce strong passwords the disclosure comes against the backdrop of php2shell set of two critical vulnerabilities in php cve 2026 109618 and cve 2026 109619 that have witnessed widespread exploitation attempts following their disclosure last week however perplexity researcher adel karimi has recorded what appears to be the first in the wild successful exploitation of the vulnerabilities to run shell commands on honeypot servers these commands have been observed using wget curl or php cli to fetch additional payloads from remote server 162 35 99 94 80 no downloaded second stage artifacts have been observed so far found this article title: PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw
cleaned_text: php has rebuilt its official windows packages for php through to fix cve 2026 111497 flaw in the brotli compression library that the packages include the flaw can let an attacker corrupt memory and potentially run code php says the flaw can be reached through the curl extension when the extension decompresses http responses automatically curl leaves that off by default but applications and http client libraries can turn it on the rebuilt packages numbered 12 27 36 and 35 come five days after the october 21 releases that fixed the two php2shell remote code execution flaws they use the same php source so those fixes stay in place and they now include brotli the fixed version php publishes software bill of materials list of the components inside with each package for last week x64 non thread safe builds of all four versions those lists show brotli one of the affected versions php advises windows users to install the new builds from its downloads page because the php version itself is unchanged php shows the same number before and after the in the file name as in php 12 nts win32 vs17 x64 zip and the sha 256 hash listed on the downloads page identify the new build automatic decompression means curl asks the server for compressed response and unpacks it in php code the curlopt encoding option turns it on and an empty value accepts every format curl supports guzzle php http client library sets that empty value by default for requests it sends through curl according to the code in its 16 release and in based on that code and php own description an application that keeps guzzle default settings meets the condition for reaching the flaw on last week windows builds the hacker news has not tested this on windows system an attack would come as crafted compressed response from server that the php application contacts google rates the flaw out of 10 or critical on the cvss scale red hat rates it or important on the cvss scale imperva researchers ran code through the flaw on one official node js build and it took them several attempts php notice does not mention any attacks cisa assessment of october 23 recorded no exploitation and the flaw was not in its known exploited vulnerabilities catalog as of that day update researchers at openai found the flaw google fixed it in brotli and 10 when it was first disclosed on october 21 node js bun and other software that ships its own copy of brotli have also released fixes php notice offers no workaround for systems that cannot be updated yet openai advises turning off automatic brotli decompression in http clients until the update is installed and warns that removing br brotli name in the accept encoding header alone does not stop server from sending it in php code following that advice means not setting curlopt encoding because curl does not decompress responses without it in guzzle it means setting the decode content request option to false which stops all automatic decoding so gzip responses also arrive compressed found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
cleaned_text: cybersecurity researchers are calling attention to what they say is recurring social engineering pattern across hundreds of cases in which threat actors use microsoft teams external chat creation feature to conduct impersonation scams or to deliver malware consistent pattern of attacker behavior has emerged across these incidents the use of the same throwaway tenants the same it support internal display names the same remote access tools and increasingly the same payload domains arctic wolf labs said in report shared with the hacker news the attacks consistently employ it themed display names or friendly sounding first names to subvert external user warnings in teams these messages originate from teams identities established through newly created or acquired microsoft 365 tenants nearly 30 40 of the cases investigated by the cybersecurity company involve the use of onmicrosoft com permanent fallback domain automatically generated by microsoft when microsoft 365 tenant is created these domains masquerade as it infrastructure opting for help desk or support themed word as the tenant name to increase their credibility helpdeskteam365 onmicrosoft com itendpoint365 onmicrosoft com itcoreportal onmicrosoft com itadmin922 onmicrosoft com corporateitservicellc onmicrosoft com as observed in many cases before these teams sessions are preceded by mail bombing where the victim inbox is flooded with hundreds of newsletter or subscription confirmations in short span of time the approach is designed to induce false sense of urgency with the teams it support message arriving soon after to help resolve the problem some of the display names observed by arctic wolf across different cases are listed below help desk it support helpdesk manager it service desk liam it service desk liam it service desk matt it service desk scott it support christopher thomas helpdesk supervisor enterprise it security internal it tech support internal business it solutions support internal maintenance service it representative it help desk in recent iterations the attackers have been observed adding the target organization domain or company name in their display name to lend the messages additional legitimacy we also observed recent shift toward paid top level domains tlds for tenant creation arctic wolf said of the paid domains we identified in these types of scams over the past few months approximately 50 percent of fake identities used the top tld around 40 percent used standard com domain and just over five percent used multi level domains such as com pl com vn and com br the activity aligns with that of stac4749 has history of creating it themed cloud domains under the top tld and leveraging plausible employee usernames to make the accounts appear authentic these attacks have led to the deployment of chaos ransomware according to sophos the attacks specifically go after organizations where external access is enabled this also involves an element of vishing to trick victims to granting them hands on keyboard access through legitimate remote monitoring and management rmm tool like quick assist anydesk screenconnect connectwise teamviewer atera zoho assist netsupport and logmein the remote access is abused to conduct reconnaissance deliver additional payloads like the gogrpc backdoor facilitate lateral movement to domain controllers and deploy additional rmm tools like level for redundancy before exfiltrating sensitive data and dropping the ransomware binary in subset of cases attackers leveraged microsoft notes arctic wolf said attackers generally avoid pasting url directly into teams which would trigger safe links zap scanning and instead navigate to the payload themselves during the remote session consequently endpoint and identity telemetry are essential monitoring surfaces alongside message scanning in one case identified by the cybersecurity vendor the threat actor is said to have instructed the user to run powershell command to download file and then launch it the powershell command is designed to download an msi installer from microsoft azure blob storage when the victim runs the installer it launches powershell script responsible for extracting and executing python implant embedded within it the backdoor then runs another msi transaction that issues ldap queries to active directory for all computer and user objects and then transmits the information to an external server external microsoft teams chat has become an effective initial access vector because it exploits trust rather than software vulnerability arctic wolf said across the activity examined attackers combined email bombing convincing it support impersonation newly created tenants and domains and rapid social engineering to move victims from seemingly routine chat to remote access payload execution and in some cases broader compromise found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter title: Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes
cleaned_text: two critical flaws in wasmtime webassembly runtime that can be built into other software could allow malicious webassembly module to escape the sandbox intended to contain it the project maintainers say an attacker would first need vulnerable wasmtime build to compile module they control and one of the flaws affects only arm64 systems fixed versions were released on october 19 and 20 and the maintainers have not reported any attacks wasmtime runs webassembly code outside web browsers both bugs are in cranelift the compiler it uses by default to turn webassembly into machine code wasmtime maintainers at the bytecode alliance rated each flaw out of 10 on the cvss scale in advisories published on october 19 cve 2026 115889 affects wasmtime across all processor architectures cve 2026 115893 affects only arm64 also called aarch64 the sandbox is meant to keep module inside set limits module can only use its own memory and the host functions it is given and its code can only jump to checked locations because both flaws need module the attacker controls the risk is highest for services that compile modules written by other people fastly for example says its compute platform runs customer code using wasmtime the advisories do not name any affected services or specify what an attacker could access after escaping the sandbox neither flaw was in the known exploited vulnerabilities catalog kept by the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency cisa as of october 26 which versions are affected the two flaws were fixed at different times so whether your version is affected depends on your release line and for one flaw your processor architecture wasmtime version cve 2026 115889 any architecture cve 2026 115893 arm64 only what to do before 36 19 includes 24 affected affected update to 36 19 or move to 48 49 or 50 36 19 fixed fixed none needed for these flaws 37 through 42 affected affected move to 48 49 or 50 43 through 47 not affected affected move to 48 49 or 50 48 through 48 not affected affected update to 48 48 not affected fixed none needed for these flaws 49 through 49 not affected affected update to 49 49 and 50 or later not affected fixed none needed for these flaws wasmtime supports long term support lts releases which are numbered in multiples of 12 for two years other releases get two months security fixes are guaranteed for supported releases only the 36 48 49 and 50 release lines are still supported every other line including the 24 lts line whose support ended on august 20 2026 got no fix arm64 hosts that updated to 36 42 or 43 in april to fix an earlier cranelift sandbox escape on arm64 are still affected by cve 2026 115893 what to do update to the fixed release for your line 36 19 48 or 49 wasmtime 50 released on october 20 is fixed for both flaws hosts on an unsupported line need to move to one of these releases wasmtime can be built into other programs as library so updating the command line tool does not fix them each program that includes wasmtime needs to be rebuilt with fixed version neither advisory lists workaround until host is updated the risk comes from any module an outsider can supply both flaws are listed in rustsec the database the cargo audit tool uses to check cargo lock files as rustsec 2026 0380 and rustsec 2026 0379 as of october 26 github advisory database had reviewed entry for cve 2026 115889 but none for cve 2026 115893 github says only reviewed entries trigger dependabot alerts so dependabot users should not expect an alert for the arm64 flaw spin an open source tool for building serverless webassembly apps that runs on wasmtime moved to wasmtime 50 in version on october 21 how the two flaws work cve 2026 115889 comes from how cranelift stored the numbers it uses to track values inside function before version 43 it packed these numbers into 24 bit fields and in release builds number too large for its field overflowed without any error cranelift could then refer to the wrong value producing incorrect machine code very large webassembly function or one crafted to use many values can use this to force type confusion and escape the sandbox according to the advisory wasmtime main development line had already removed the problem change merged on february 18 widened the fields to 32 bits and shipped in wasmtime 43 on march 20 its description presented it as way to compile larger functions and did not mention security the 36 lts line got the same change on october 19 the advisory does not say when the security impact was recognized cve 2026 115893 involves br table webassembly instruction that jumps to one of many places in the code based on an index an index outside the table goes to default target on arm64 cranelift sent these out of range indexes to the default with branch that can only reach about mib br table with more than about 256 000 targets made the jump table too big for that reach so the branch silently pointed to the wrong place any wasmtime engine on arm64 with default settings can be forced to jump to arbitrary code by user controlled wasm module the advisory says the bug has been present since wasmtime first supported arm64 in 2020 the fix sends out of range indexes through the jump table itself so no long branch is needed fixed versions also refuse to compile br table with more than 65 520 targets found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Between alerts: What Attackers Do in the Spaces Ordinary Detection Misses
cleaned_text: every soc struggles with pile of alerts very few of those alerts explain how an attack started or how it progressed network data like that from network detection and response ndr platform connects individual alerts into one timeline and it feeds the defensive systems that can tie all events together into one coordinated view soc teams often first see the shape of an intrusion through series of smaller alerts that are triggered when signature matches known malware hash threshold flags an unusual spike in failed logins or an endpoint agent detects suspicious activity when viewed through the siem dashboard an attack often begins as series of distinct events with related or overlapping timestamps artificial intelligence has accelerated modern attacks enabling attackers to automate reconnaissance craft targeted payloads and execute scripts in seconds yet speed does not obfuscate the need for stealth to evade detection adversaries deliberately draw out operations hide inside standard admin tooling and work in the quiet intervals between alarms adversaries might spend days or weeks inside an enterprise environment before an action generates high priority security alert when an alert finally surfaces it doesn necessarily mark the start of compromise it may in fact be one event in much longer sequence analysts who investigate only the triggering event may miss the chained activity that explains how the intrusion developed the anatomy of silent progression between initial access and high severity alert adversary activity can blend into ordinary business operations adversaries understand the operational limits of security teams and they exploit them if every dns query ldap request smb connection or authentication attempt generated an investigation soc queues would quickly become even more unmanageable tradecraft purposely takes advantage of that reality adversaries can spread reconnaissance across hours or distributed sources instead of launching an obvious scan they may use compromised account to query domain controller over ldap at modest pace to map users groups and systems handful of kerberos service ticket requests can yield credentials to crack offline well outside the soc view valid credentials then open the door to smb or rdp the same services administrators rely on every day and the attacker moves from host to host files may be gathered on one internal system and compressed later that system may reach an external destination over https or dns at regular intervals with just enough variation in timing to resemble normal traffic as it exfiltrates data each step borrows something the business already depends on while individual actions may not necessarily look suspicious their significance often emerges from relationships and sequences for instance host that communicates with new system once may be unremarkable host that queries several internal services authenticates to peer establishes an smb session and then connects to an external destination presents different investigative picture the activity becomes more meaningful when viewed across time when siloed tools see only slices of this type of transaction they might miss the bigger picture context only becomes readily apparent when activities and signals are combined and correlated via network observation what more attackers increasingly use ai to automate reconnaissance and move faster defenders need to apply ai to the same problem but it needs detailed network evidence from an ndr to search the evidence between the alerts secops teams don have to turn detection thresholds down and drown analysts in more alerts just to spot adversary activity doing so would be untenable anyway soc can investigate every dns query authentication request or connection as though it were an incident in addition many teams operate with tools that show an alert fired yet offer sparse detail on how the activity behind it unfolded to prevent blindspots soc teams can retain the underlying network telemetry so an analyst can go back and review what happened when an alert outage or other signal gives them reason to look however that requires more than knowing when two systems exchanged traffic protocol aware network data from an ndr platform can show the kind of interaction that took place who or what participated when it happened and how that relationship evolved over time for instance if workstation triggers an endpoint alert at 14 the alert may show an analyst what happened on the endpoint at that moment network evidence from an ndr can extend the timeline and answer few crucial questions was the workstation querying an unusual domain earlier that day did it authenticate to another system or establish smb connections to internal peers did those systems communicate with additional hosts did the workstation later establish an encrypted session with an external destination each individual event may have perfectly legitimate explanations it only in combination though that the sequence provides different level of context for an investigator that context helps establish whether the endpoint event was an isolated problem or one discrete stage in broader progression for an ai assisted investigation the context derived from ndr provides the evidence needed to search for related activity across hosts users protocols and time rather than treating each alert as separate event why this matters for the ai soc ai in the soc changes the economics of an investigation while human analyst has to decide which systems users sessions and time periods deserve attention an ai assisted soc can search across that same breadth of evidence much faster bringing relevant data into one view in minutes rather than hours correlation and analysis can happen asynchronously allowing analysts to review and query broader set of data much sooner when ai handles the synthesis the process of identifying patterns is faster still when an attacker is patient methodically timing actions across longer periods evidence might be spread across hundreds of seemingly ordinary transactions since human analyst can reasonably manually investigate each piece of evidence the more practical approach is to construct an automated workflow in an ndr platform to identify context and look for relationships then give the analyst the evidence so they can make judgement call the outcome is more activity examined across more systems over longer period the benefits are time savings manual work is significantly reduced clearer insights more context can be surfaced by advanced algorithms searching across thousands of data points better decisions analysts can focus on making strategic risk decisions instead of picking apart pieces of alerts the same process can help with operational issues if an application goes down for example network telemetry will show which services were communicating where communications began to fail which dependencies were affected and what changed around the event if the cause turns out to be malicious the investigation already has record of the activity beyond individual alerts alerts give analysts place to start an investigation they do not necessarily explain what happened before it what happened after it what happening simultaneously or whether other activity in the environment is related issues that appear routine in isolation may look very different when data is correlated and context is added network telemetry provides the surrounding evidence needed to build critical context protocol aware data from the ndr preserves the details of network interactions including both ends of communication the protocols and services involved timestamps for those interactions and how interactions change over time it the telemetry that gives automated investigation workflows broader body of evidence to work from when triaging high priority alert with evidence available for automated analysis ai agents can correlate activity over time connect communications between systems and surface sequences that would otherwise remain separate innocuous looking events the ability to apply context across disparate communications and sequences is what allows soc teams to find the riskiest activity without this evidence individual alerts and sequences may continue to present as harmless attackers have already identified the opportunity now it time for defenders to apply the same principles and keep up about corelight your ai soc is only as effective as the data behind it title: Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations
cleaned_text: cybersecurity researchers have disclosed microsoft 365 campaign that has been observed leveraging an adversary in the middle aitm relay to capture sign in sessions and then replay the stolen tokens to break into email accounts at 79 organizations huntress which observed the activity between july 14 and september 22 2026 said it detected 497 successful microsoft 365 sign in events across the victim organizations from over 200 000 login attempts with the attackers ultimately compromising 97 accounts and registering 48 rogue entra devices rather than guessing passwords the attacker replayed sign in tokens stolen from victims and we ve traced more than 200 000 failed login attempts from the campaign window back to the 193 26 115 24 ip range huntress researchers andrea hatcher susannah matt matt poto and andrew schwartz said the attack has been found to employ an aitm login page which sits between the victims and legitimate microsoft infrastructure to capture the entered credentials and mfa codes and relay the information to the real login page the end goal is to collect the access token issued by microsoft following the sign in process so that it doesn have to bypass mfa second time the proof of login token is subsequently replayed by the attacker from their own devices within minutes to conduct automated sign in attempts against microsoft 365 services the approach has been codenamed token spraying as it involves the attacker replaying many stolen tokens at scale across several organizations in manner that analogous to password spraying upon gaining successful access the attackers moved to add their own authenticator app as form of persistence to complete mfa challenges for new sign ins and overcome scenarios where the stolen session token expires or gets revoked by the victim in no less than 19 organizations the victim existing mfa methods were removed and new method registered within three hours of the first sign in in one case observed on july 21 2026 the threat actors activated new authenticator app named iphone 13 less than 51 minutes after the session was hijacked rogue devices served the same purpose the researchers said the threat actor registered at least 48 fake computers in victim organizations microsoft directories registered device can give the attacker more durable way to request tokens than the stolen session alone and it stays in the directory until someone deletes it furthermore the attackers have also been spotted setting up hidden email rules in victims inboxes with names such as sss ss it and to delete incoming mail with certain keywords referencing payroll deposit and bonus or move them to obscure folders like rss feeds and conversation history in one compromised mailbox the email rule marked all incoming messages as read and deleted them the mailbox was then used to send outbound spam to hundreds of external recipients before microsoft entra id protection rated the account high risk huntress said the tokens originate from multiple sources including aitm relays behind fake sign in pages device code phishing and social engineering during legitimate login process the campaign was first observed from romanian ip address 193 26 115 221 which according to virustotal is used by remote access trojan called asyncrat the ip address is associated with german hosting provider named 1337 services gmbh data from greynoise currently lists 29 ip addresses matching the hosting provider out of which 10 have been flagged as malicious and five are marked suspicious notably the entity is linked to starkrdp and rdp sh which allows paying customers to rent virtual servers the domains tied to both starkrdp and rdp sh were taken down alongside websites for nulled cracked and sellix as part of an international law enforcement operation dubbed talent in january 2025 as of writing the two platforms are operational with the former now rebranded as exy sh starkrdp has always been operating by the law and is not involved in any of these alleged crimes and the legal process will confirm this the starkrdp telegram account said in post dated january 30 according to independent cybersecurity journalist brian krebs the only things that were seized is sic the website server and our domain unfortunately no one can tell who took it and with whom we can talk about it therefore we will restart operation soon under different name to close the chapter of starkrdp organizations who suspect token replay compromise are recommended to revoke sessions and reset the password audit entra devices review mfa methods check for unexpected inbox rules or new enterprise applications and restrict device code workflow with conditional access policies conditional access policies cap can help fill some of the security gaps that mfa can as long as they re appropriately implemented huntress researchers said businesses setting up caps should require mfa or block for all users all cloud apps and all client app types unconditionally found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
cleaned_text: an automated campaign is using stolen github tokens to plant workflows that print repository secrets into its github actions logs which the attackers then download before deleting the runs the attacks have succeeded in private repositories and github enterprise environments according to an analysis by cloud security company wiz github safeguard that pauses suspicious workflow runs stopped every public repository run wiz checked but it does not cover private repositories or github enterprise server each workflow sits on new branch named ci sync followed by six random characters deleting branch or the run it started does not undo the exposure every secret the repository could read should be rotated and the token that pushed the branch revoked wiz has tracked the campaign since september 15 and calls it gheist after the user agent gheist that the attackers tool sends with github api requests wiz has recovered more than 13 500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts from personal projects to the private repositories of enterprise organizations wiz analysis does not say how many organizations had secrets exposed in private repositories and on github enterprise server github audit logs show runs on the planted branches finishing and then being deleted by the gheist user agent aws cloudtrail logs show the organization own workflows also running on those branches and assuming aws roles sign that github actions ran there without approval in enterprise organizations the tool cycled through tokens from several users and automation accounts within minutes and cloned private repositories before planting the workflow hours later cloud credentials from the same organization were used to enumerate aws secrets manager wiz analysis does not say where those credentials came from or who used them as of october 24 the campaign was still running and changing about two thirds of the accounts involved were no longer available on github wiz reported the activity to github and says their disappearance likely reflects response anyone with write access to github repository can read every secret configured in it according to github documentation stolen token with that access is enough for each repository token can reach the tool creates ci sync branch and commits one file github workflows sync check yml with the message ci sync config the commit is unsigned and includes the token owner name pushing it starts the workflow the workflow prints the job environment and every secret the job can read encoded in base32 github masks secrets in logs but its documentation says this is not guaranteed once value has been encoded or otherwise changed wiz says the base32 text no longer matches the original secret so it prints in full the workflow sets an empty permissions block that limits the job github token which the attackers do not need and does not stop the job from reading secrets one version of the tool also runs job for each deployment environment in the repository so secrets limited to those environments print too these are often production credentials according to wiz the tool then downloads the log through github api and deletes the run seconds later because the secrets leave through github itself there is no attacker server or outbound connection to block since july 28 github has held workflow runs it identifies as potentially malicious until collaborator with write access approves them github says the hold currently applies to public repositories on github com only and that github enterprise server does not have it at this time every public gheist run wiz checked across all versions of the tool was still waiting for approval so its payload never ran the hold only catches runs that github flags new variant of ghostaction separate campaign ran in public repositories until github began blocking it on october according to research from security company gitguardian wiz says gheist is distinct from ghostaction which uses different workflow files around october 19 one version of the tool began pushing second job meant for self hosted runners the machines organizations run themselves to process github actions jobs it appears to target only repositories that have such runner registered the job is written to search the runner machine for credentials including 31 types of tokens private keys process environments aws instance role credentials runner credential files and the kubernetes service account token wiz describes the job as buggy and its analysis reports no successful run the sources wiz could trace for the stolen tokens include infostealer logs and tokens exposed in earlier supply chain attacks such as the march compromise of the trivy vulnerability scanner other attackers also use the same accounts on october 391 accounts many of them also used by gheist renamed about 461 repositories to appear to be cracked software and spread malware the renaming wiped 610 of the planted branches some victims also appear to be infected with polinrider malware that researchers have linked to north korea on october 19 and 20 three of them re pushed their gheist commits with loader added to vite config js file megalodon campaign that pushed secret stealing workflows into thousands of github repositories in may had also hit 57 of the accounts how to check your repositories wiz recommends these checks look for branches named ci sync followed by six characters where the only change is new github workflows sync check yml file with the commit message ci sync config in github audit logs look for workflow runs on ci sync branches that were deleted within minute of finishing and for any activity from the user agent gheist if your workflows sign in to cloud provider with oidc check cloud audit logs for role assumptions or token exchanges whose subject includes ci sync branch this works even if you do not collect github logs on self hosted runners look for the files gdmp pat gdmp patg and gdmp sweep and the string gdmp pivot in job logs oidc lets workflows sign in with short lived tokens instead of stored cloud keys by default token subject includes the branch name only when the job does not use deployment environment according to github oidc documentation the published indicators are user agent gheist branch ci sync 9a commit message ci sync config adding only github workflows sync check yml string tojson secrets base32 120 string gdmp pivot file gdmp pat file gdmp patg file gdmp sweep git blob sha plain workflow f3da2b8b357dcda02fd455d314be2a95007516a6 git blob sha timeout version d09535857a741bbb976bdc084a9a021713133291 git blob sha separator version 1dc5af9cce950aad1eb1546ecce8565b117540c4 git blob sha self hosted job version c665b778b2d822453293003e7ca0bbb2cb08e39d versions of the workflow that list repository deployment environments vary by repository so they have no fixed hash what to do if you find ci sync branch wiz advises these steps for an affected repository rotate every repository organization and environment secret the repository could use revoke the tokens that pushed the commits and check their owners devices for infostealers if ci sync branch ran on self hosted runner treat the machine and its cloud instance role as compromised do not approve held sync check runs and do not run code from ci sync branches to make stolen token less useful wiz also recommends these steps require reviewers on environments that hold production secrets limit oidc trust policies to protected branches or environments use github apps or short lived fine grained tokens instead of personal access tokens run self hosted runners as short lived machines without docker socket access or open access to cloud metadata job cannot read an environment secrets until required reviewer approves it according to github documentation found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter title: Malicious File in Downloads Folder Tries to Trick AI Coding Agent Into Installing Malware
cleaned_text: malicious instruction file sitting in developer downloads folder tried to make their ai coding agent install known malicious npm package security firm forever security said in report published last week the company caught the attempt on real customer machine and stopped the agent before any code ran it could not determine how the file got into the folder the file was agents md plain text instructions file that coding agent such as openai codex reads when it starts in folder and follows as directions it was dressed up as ordinary engineering notes one section told the agent to add server to its own configuration and install package called function color from npm that package is part of malware campaign that other researchers have documented separately function color pulls in downloader called function flag which fetches and runs windows payload researchers at cloudsek and checkmarx who analyzed the campaign named it malfex two things each harmless on its own make this work forever said an agent is built to trust and obey the instructions file in the folder it opens and web page can save file to the downloads folder on its own without click or permission prompt choosing the name and contents put together web page can drop file the agent will treat as orders into folder the agent trusts researchers did not establish that this is how the file was caught to title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
cleaned_text: the goahead embedded web server loaded certificate revocation list into its default tls backend but never turned revocation checking on so revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups the flaw is in builds that use the openssl backend with mutual tls where the server checks client certificate and vice versa and revocation list is configured to block revoked certificates that is setup an operator turns on deliberately default build does not goahead released to device makers on august 2026 and publicly published on october 12 fixes it goahead is small web server that device makers build into firmware to run management pages on routers printers gateways and industrial controllers its maker embedthis says it runs in hundreds of millions of devices the flaw was found by bastien ry of foxio who described it and two other tls problems in write up on october 26 on an affected build the server loads the revocation list file at startup and reports no error so an operator who configured it has every reason to think revocation is working it is not client whose certificate was revoked for example stolen or retired device completes the handshake as if the certificate were still valid and gets whatever access that identity allows in foxio test against goahead with openssl revoked certificate was accepted with issuer checking switched on the openssl advisory describes revoked client certificates as silently accepted to be exploited the build must use the openssl backend with client certificates required trusted certificate authority bundle and issuer checking enabled and revocation list configured the attacker must hold certificate signed by trusted authority and listed as revoked builds that use the mbed tls backend are unaffected that backend checks revocation via separate code path the identifier on the advisory is cve 2026 115881 rated by embedthis as of october 27 that identifier and the others below were not yet live in the public cve and nvd databases embedthis says it has requested them the severity ratings are the vendor own researchers cover two further problems each tied to specific tls build the versions and fixes differ so the table below maps each by backend tls build what goes wrong affected versions fix or interim option openssl default revocation list loaded but never enforced revoked client certificates accepted cve 2026 115881 rated through upgrade to no interim option in the advisory libressl legacy verifier client certificate chain longer than the limit is accepted when client certificates are required but issuer checking is off cve 2026 115884 rated and earlier on those libressl versions upgrade to or turn issuer checking on with trusted ca bundle or use openssl or libressl mbed tls length typo sends byte diffie hellman value instead of the full 2048 bit one so passive observer can decrypt the session rated no cve assigned through upgrade to turn off finite field dhe suites or use the openssl backend the mbed tls problem only reaches session if the client accepts the broken setup openssl current go current java and mainstream browsers refuse value that small and fall back to stronger key exchange so the session never completes clients without minimum size check such as some embedded or custom ones accept it and then anyone who recorded the traffic can work out the key and read the session tls and ecdhe sessions are unaffected and mbed tls removed the key exchange they rely on the libressl problem allows an attacker to present certificate chain longer than goahead 10 certificate limit and still complete the handshake as an authenticated client without any trusted key it appears only on builds linked against the older libressl versions listed above and only where client certificates are required with issuer checking off openssl boringssl aws lc and libressl reject the over long chain which backend and settings build uses are chosen when the firmware is compiled so device owner cannot tell from the outside which apply that is also why the fix is slow to arrive goahead is drop in replacement that device makers rebuild and ship as firmware update and an owner gets it only when their manufacturer does so whether any manufacturer has shipped it is not known as of october 27 no source reported any of these problems being used in attacks embedthis policy is to end disclosure embargo and publish early if flaw is being exploited or disclosed by someone else so the coordinated october 12 release is consistent with no known attacks however it does not prove there are none embedthis notifies customers of security updates through its builder portal foxio has published proof of concept code and offers fingerprints through its ja4scan tool to find goahead servers by backend the tool is free but its source is available only on request and fingerprint identifies build not confirmed vulnerable server none of the device makers embedthis lists as goahead users which include hp oracle siemens canon rockwell link and comcast has been shown to run an affected backend and setting the affected population is not established the same release closes 11 advisories in all three of them rated critical one is login bypass on build using http basic or form login an attacker who knows valid username can sign in with any password if that user stored password is in the newer blowfish format which goahead added in version embedthis says form login is the default for its built in administration pages after upgrading embedthis recommends ending active sessions restarting the server and changing blowfish stored passwords found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
cleaned_text: microsoft has fixed flaw in its authenticator app for android that let malicious app with no permissions pose as trusted microsoft app such as teams and collect sign in tokens for victim work account microsoft tracks the flaw as cve 2026 80097 and fixed it in authenticator for android version 2606 4246 so anyone using the app should update in the researchers tests the tokens gave full access to the account email files and calendar microsoft says exploitation also needs the victim to complete sign in step in authenticator and that the flaw has not been used in attacks the research comes from ofek levin working through fellowship program at the security firm enclave which published the technical details on october 23 2026 microsoft assigned the cve on september and rated it on the cvss scale which it labels important on android authenticator does more than show six digit codes it also acts as broker when teams outlook or another microsoft app needs to sign user in it asks authenticator and authenticator hands back token digital pass that proves the user is logged in because the broker controls access to the entire account it should be careful about which app it grants token to the flaw let the wrong app get one authenticator exposes component an activity named accountchooseractivity that any app on the device can start when the attacker app started it authenticator built its token request from values the attacker app supplied including the name of the app it claimed to be the app said it was teams and the broker believed it signature check was supposed to stop this but it did not the check looked up the real signature of the app being impersonated and confirmed the request matched it because teams was genuinely installed on the device its real signature was there to read so the check passed authenticator could also see which app had actually made the request enclave found but it did not use that to decide whether to hand over token in enclave tests posing as teams and requesting microsoft graph tokens returned permissions to read and send mail read and write files and read and write calendars among others microsoft describes the result more generally successful attacker could authenticate as the signed in user and reach that user resources the tokens apply to the work account signed into authenticator on that device not to other accounts the two accounts disagree on one point reader should weigh enclave reported that its proof of concept returned tokens without any user interaction other than the presence of signed in account microsoft advisory says exploitation requires installing malicious app on the device and convincing the user to complete an authentication flow in authenticator its cvss score also indicates that the flaw requires user interaction microsoft says the flaw has not been exploited and was not publicly disclosed before the fix and rates exploitation as less likely it was part of the company september 2026 patch tuesday and was not one of the two windows flaws flagged that month as already under attack the vulnerability is not listed in the cisa known exploited vulnerabilities catalog as of october 26 2026 the fix is to update microsoft authenticator for android to version 2606 4246 or later as linked in microsoft advisory organizations that manage android devices can require that minimum version through their device management microsoft advisory gives the fix but does not say whether updating cancels any token malicious app may already have obtained so that remains unclear from the title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key

key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify keystone buyer who trusted counterfeit could have their crypto stolen but the incident did not involve owners recovery phrases or wallet private keys keystone will destroy 18 835 unsold devices that carry the key and all new devices will get new one keystone found the unauthorized access on october 20 and its possibility that it is counterfeit owners of such device should contact keystone support and use it only after the company confirms it is genuine device delivered before october 20 that passes the check can be considered genuine and used normally according to keystone the company has not said when the attacker first got in the attacker exploited vulnerability in third party data monitoring tool used by keystone website to escalate privileges according to the company that let the attacker obtain customer data and the key keystone blocked the attacker access on october 20 and has since fixed the vulnerability it has not said where the key was stored how the device check works the owner scans qr code on keystone verification page with the device then enters the code the device displays on the page in keystone open source firmware the qr code carries that code in encrypted form and the device decrypts it with its stored key so correct code shows that the device holds the key the key is used only for this check it plays no part in creating recovery phrases deriving private keys or signing transactions anyone with copy of the key could produce the right codes so counterfeit device carrying it could pass the check such devices could be sold or shipped to customers leading to the theft of their crypto keystone said the company has not reported any counterfeit devices or thefts the key is written into each device during manufacturing and cannot be erased or rewritten the firmware keeps it in memory which can be written only once and refuses to accept second key so devices already made cannot be switched to the new key customer records keystone first disclosed the breach on october 24 saying third party had obtained customers shipping information the incident affected 25 964 buyer records from purchases on keystone website between 2024 and 2026 the company said on october 26 the records hold names contact details shipping addresses and order details keystone online store runs on shopify which stored and managed the records payment card and bank details and government id numbers were not involved keystone said purchase records from amazon and keystone other sales channels were not affected keystone has also included 12 873 unpaid checkout records in its response as precaution these hold names contact details and shipping information from purchases that were never completed some of the affected data should already have been deleted keystone had promised to delete shipping information 180 days after each order an automated tool keystone built to erase records in bulk did not work reliably some deletions failed and keystone did not catch the failures in time keystone is shortening the period it retains customers personal data from 180 days to 90 days effective immediately it has asked shopify to delete buyers personal data older than 90 days and expects that to be done on november as of october 27 its privacy policy still listed 180 days keystone is emailing affected customers and plans page where people can check whether their information was affected what keystone owners should do keystone guidance covers these situations delivered before october 20 device that passes the check can be used normally received after october 20 with the old key do not use the device until keystone support at support keyst one confirms it is genuine title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
cleaned_text: fake login pages are nothing new but generative ai is making them easier to build and more convincing attackers can recreate familiar login screens impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords they can also capture mfa codes or hijack authenticated sessions allowing attackers to gain access to corporate accounts even when additional security measures are in place how ai is making fake login pages more convincing attackers have long used fake login pages to steal credentials but generative ai makes it easier to create convincing replicas of legitimate authentication portals from company logos and page layouts to login prompts these fraudulent pages can closely resemble the websites employees regularly access ai also makes it easier to tailor phishing campaigns to specific organizations or employees for example attackers can create personalized it notifications that direct employees to fraudulent login page using the company branding and familiar authentication prompts these attacks often rely on lookalike domains that closely resemble legitimate web addresses with subtle spelling changes or additional characters combined with realistic login pages and targeted messaging these tactics make phishing attempts harder to recognize while these techniques aren new generative ai lets attackers create customize and adapt phishing campaigns more quickly and at larger scale the 2026 verizon data breach investigations report found that phishing accounted for 44 of the ai assisted initial access techniques examined how fake login pages lead to account takeovers fake login pages can capture more than usernames and passwords some replicate multi step authentication processes to collect mfa codes which attackers can attempt to use before they expire to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts and applications more sophisticated attacks use adversary in the middle aitm techniques to intercept authentication sessions in these attacks fraudulent website acts as proxy between the user and the legitimate service relaying authentication requests in real time after the user successfully authenticates the attacker may capture session cookie or authentication token and use it to access the account without completing another mfa challenge this makes session hijacking particularly dangerous even with mfa enabled attackers can potentially access accounts by stealing active session tokens this lets them hijack an authenticated session without entering password or completing another mfa challenge why traditional phishing defenses aren always enough security awareness training helps employees recognize phishing attempts but convincing login page replicas can be difficult to distinguish from legitimate websites even experienced users can overlook subtle warning signs particularly when fraudulent page uses familiar branding and authentication prompts email filters url blocklists and website reputation services can stop many known phishing threats but newly registered domains and short lived phishing sites may evade detection attackers also distribute malicious links through text messages collaboration platforms and search ads letting phishing attempts bypass email based defenses url inspection provides another layer of protection but lookalike domains can be difficult to identify valid https connection also doesn guarantee that website is legitimate these gaps highlight the need for security controls that can evaluate suspicious websites and detect potential credential harvesting attempts before users enter their login information how organizations can protect against credential theft organizations can reduce the risk of credential theft by strengthening authentication detecting suspicious login pages and limiting what attackers can access if an account is compromised use phishing resistant mfa and passkeys fido2 security keys and passkeys use cryptographic authentication tied to legitimate website domains reducing the risk of credential theft through fraudulent login pages implement browser level phishing protection browser based security tools can detect look alike domains brand impersonation and suspicious url patterns ai powered detection can help identify credential harvesting sites and warn users before they enter sensitive information monitor authentication and session activity unusual sign in locations unfamiliar devices and suspicious session behavior can indicate account compromise continuous monitoring helps security teams identify and respond to potential account takeovers limit privileged access enforcing least privilege policies and removing unnecessary standing privileges limits what attackers can access through compromised accounts just in time access further reduces the window of opportunity for abusing elevated permissions establish phishing response procedures organizations should have clear processes for reporting suspected phishing attempts revoking compromised sessions resetting credentials and investigating unauthorized access protecting credentials before they re exposed phishing protection needs to extend beyond email filters and traditional detection methods to the point where users enter their credentials keeper ai powered phishing protection uses on device ai to identify suspicious websites including look alike domains and spoofed login pages warning users before they enter their credentials by identifying suspicious websites earlier organizations can reduce opportunities for credential harvesting and prevent stolen credentials from leading to account takeovers note this article has been expertly written and contributed by aranza trevino at keeper security found this article interesting this article is contributed piece from one of our valued partners follow us on google news twitter and title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
cleaned_text: openai compaction feature which shrinks long conversation to save space could be turned into way to copy model hidden reasoning out in plain text security firm xint has shown openai reasoning models work through problem before answering and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read the method got past the protections openai added in august against this kind of reasoning theft openai confirmed the problem and fixed it on october 23 according to xint xint ran the technique against gpt sol one of openai reasoning models using math and algorithm puzzles its researchers wrote themselves the reasoning it pulled out came from those same requests and xint did not claim the method could reach another user reasoning xint says it cannot prove the copied text is word for word the model real reasoning because it never had the original to compare against two cheaper models each repeated the item and produced the same text which rules out mistakes in the copying step but leaves open the possibility that compaction reworded the text compaction is an openai feature that uses model to squeeze long conversation into smaller encrypted item that carries the context forward xint sent task to gpt sol and kept the encrypted reasoning it returned it then called the compaction step on the same model and told it to copy that reasoning into the compacted item word for word with every space changed to tab to get past openai usage policy filters because compaction items can move between models xint passed the item to the cheaper gpt and gpt 4o models and asked each to repeat its input exactly which they did the method worked around fix openai had already shipped in august researchers behind paper called stolen thoughts showed that encrypted reasoning from strong model could be replayed into weaker model from the same company which would then repeat it as plain text openai and others blocked that cross model replay soon after compaction got past that block xint said because the compaction step runs on the same model that made the reasoning so it never triggers the cross model check the idea built on xint earlier work called ghostcompact which showed the compaction step can be pushed to run tasks of the attacker choosing xint has published the code in its github repository the fix was on openai side so developers who build on the api do not need to change anything xint called it an undisclosed fix and said openai paid the researchers 000 reward xint tested only gpt sol and did not check whether gpt astra openai newer model is affected it is not known whether anyone used the method before openai closed it xint also argued that fixing this one path may not be enough because in its view any server side step that reads model decrypted reasoning and follows the user instructions could leak it openai keeps raw reasoning hidden partly to stop distillation where one company trains cheaper model on another outputs raw reasoning makes better training data than the final answer alone because it shows how the model worked through the problem which is what makes it worth stealing for rival openai said in september that it had disrupted july campaign that tried to expose its models hidden reasoning and linked core part of it to people associated with china moonshot ai anthropic and joint government advisory have each reported china based labs targeting the hidden reasoning of american models none of that is tied to xint compaction method which is demonstration rather than an attack consider the device secure cert ua said authentication barriers are overcome by leveraging weak or known passwords or by exploiting authentication bypass vulnerabilities in outdated firmware versions such as cve 2021 33044 and cve 2021 33045 cert ua has shared the following indicators of compromise associated with the activity presence of unknown accounts unauthorized configuration changes audit 37777 which is the default proprietary management and video streaming port used by dahua followed by collecting serial numbers breaking into those devices by employing the aforementioned two title: Volt Typhoon Used Covert Silent Train Network in Four Zero-Day Exploitation Campaigns
cleaned_text: the china nexus cyber espionage group known as volt typhoon has been attributed to now disrupted covert access network dubbed silent train that has been put to use for zero day exploitation and strategic access first identified in late 2023 silent train uses rotating chains of compromised soho iot and enterprise infrastructure lumen technologies black lotus labs said in report shared with the hacker news it employs anti forensic techniques compartmentalized operations and post operation cleanup to minimize detection and attribution its main purpose is to facilitate critical attack phases like vulnerability exploitation credential access data exfiltration and to maintain continued access to victim environments the activity stands out for two main reasons it singled out entities that could provide scalable access to downstream customers sensitive networks or strategic programs it targeted endpoint management platforms network management systems sd wan orchestrators and control plane technologies that play crucial role within enterprise environments hundreds of victims have been identified across telecommunications providers government defense contractors satellite and mission critical communication services universities it firms and critical infrastructure such as water energy transportation maritime rail aviation and emergency services volt typhoon aka bronze silhouette insidious taurus unc3236 vanguard panda and voltzite is the moniker assigned to china linked state sponsored group known for its targeting of critical infrastructure networks particularly communications energy transportation and water and wastewater systems sectors known to be active since at least 2021 the threat actor was previously observed exploiting file upload vulnerability in versa director as zero day cve 2024 39717 to deliver bespoke web shell called versamem designed to harvest credentials and enable access to downstream customers silent train session chains through multiple non and hops the latest findings from black lotus labs show that the security flaw was one among four confirmed zero day campaigns the threat actor has conducted through silent train the remaining three vulnerabilities are listed below cve 2025 8875 and cve 2025 8876 set of insecure deserialization and command injection vulnerabilities in able central cve 2026 20127 an authentication bypass vulnerability in cisco catalyst sd wan controller cve 2026 16812 an operating system command injection vulnerability in arista velocloud orchestrator separately volt typhoon is also suspected to have taken advantage of likely zero day vulnerability in quest kace before it was patched in october 2025 the campaign is estimated to have impacted more than 30 victims silent train is built around rapidly rotating chains of compromised soho iot and enterprise devices that are exploited on demand used against carefully selected targets cleaned up after each operation and continuously refreshed black lotus labs said this model has enabled volt typhoon to conduct exploitation and post exploitation operations with exceptional operational security while minimizing opportunities for detection attribution and disruption defining characteristic of these attacks is the repeated targeting of systems that can open the door to broad visibility control and access across large enterprise environments of strategic value to the what interesting is that the covert access capability began to take shape sometime around november 2023 just weeks before the first round of disruption targeting kv botnet an iot botnet linked to multiple china nexus state sponsored threat actors including volt typhoon silent train operational activity is said to have surged in the wake of the botnet second disruption in late january 2024 while simultaneously shifting to an ephemeral infrastructure comprising diverse device types and across geographies rather than continue using persistent infrastructure volt typhoon shifted to model using one time use chains of compromised devices that it could rebuild as needed black lotus labs said volt typhoon rapidly assembled and dismantled transient infrastructure creating resilient secure and compartmentalized framework that protected valuable access sector distribution of organizations targeted through silent train described as layered multi hop framework silent train is designed to let volt typhoon operators relay malicious traffic through several devices before it reaches the targets so as to obscure its origins from both victims and defenders each link in the chain serves specific purpose virtual private servers vps that function as temporary staging area and allow threat actors to provision and discard them after each session the sessions begin from vps infrastructure located outside the compromised non soho and iot devices located across different countries providers and hardware that conceal the starting point of the attack based compromised devices that function as an exit node before reaching the domestic victim and help evade geofencing and ip reputation blocklists no less than 27 device classes ranging from soho and iot devices tp link intelbras ruckus wireless sato netgear zyxel and cambium to enterprise platforms fortinet cisco prtg mirth connect and cyberpanel have been exploited and enrolled into the covert network silent train stands out for its operational discipline focusing on short lived selfmanaged sessions rather than persistent relays or c2 infrastructure black lotus labs said to construct these sessions its operators exploit exposed web interfaces on soho iot and other relay devices then deploy only the tooling needed to enable chained ssh access through the compromised node this included temporary ssh services keys configuration files and live off the land utilities at the end of operational sessions they removed every artifact and dismantled the operational chain in their wake silent train sessions lasted about four hours on average with some lasting only minutes another notable aspect is the designation of certain device types to specific positions within silent train for instance intelbras modems have been found to only appear as relay nodes while netgear orbi and fortinet fortigate appliances served as based intermediary and exit points responsible for interacting with the victim put differently the infrastructure points to deliberate compartmentalization across layers confining some device types to certain roles that remain constant while the underlying infrastructure itself changes over time so as to complicate attribution efforts by early 2025 however silent train is believed to have evolved from completely ephemeral relay network to hybrid architecture that retained enterprise grade devices for an average of one to three months instead of changing them after each engagement subsequent maturation of the platform introduced reverse tunnel variants that used open source proxies like chisel and frp to send traffic from infected devices to upstream infrastructure within the hawaii california and texas have emerged as the focus areas of silent train operations which boils down to the fact that these states host major military installations telecommunications infrastructure defense contractors satellite communications providers and critical logistics networks victimology indicates deliberate efforts to maintain access to critical ecosystems that support defense logistics communications military and civilian operations especially during heightened tensions or crises in the indo pacific region black lotus labs said the resulting picture is one of highly structured framework built to acquire protect and sustain strategic access at scale through repeated targeting of centralized management platforms and control plane technologies silent train shows how volt typhoon systematically title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
cleaned_text: chain of logic flaws with no memory corruption can turn malicious web page into code running on windows computer outside microsoft edge sandbox security researcher has shown orange tsai of devcore published the full method on october 28 five months after the chain won 175 000 at the pwn2own berlin contest in may microsoft fixed the edge bugs the day after the contest so an up to date browser is not at risk browser sandbox is the wall that keeps web page code inside the browser and off the rest of the computer breaking out of it and then running program is what turns web bug into full control of the machine browser escapes like this almost always rely on memory corruption this one used none in his write up tsai describes chain built solely from logic errors in how edge and windows handle ordinary features and he says the whole exploit is under 100 lines of code the result is universal cross site scripting uxss primitive way to run javascript on any website bypassing the content security policy meant to prevent it because the attack starts from the browser own process it can reach sites like google com that an ordinary web bug cannot touch tsai calls this new attack surface rather than one off bug this was competition exploit not an attack seen in the wild tsai demonstrated it on stage at pwn2own there is no evidence it has been used against real users and the public cve records list exploitation as none one step in the chain restarts the browser which tsai notes is convenience for the contest and not needed in real attack the chain begins with an edge feature for business sign ins called conditional access navigation throttle tsai found that triggering it lets the browser own process start new navigation that is not tied to the page that asked for it so edge attaches it to whichever tab is open that mismatch is the first bug and it produces the uxss making it run without click took four more weaknesses edge checked that the request came from trusted microsoft site but tsai bypassed the check by opening the request from second window edge popup blocker should have stopped that window but edge carried hardcoded list of allowed addresses and one of them opened the popup the attack also required the victim to be already signed in which the edge auto sign in feature provides on its own when the user visits microsoft site lastly the chain reads the victim email address from microsoft site assets msn com which returned it to any website due to misconfigured cross origin setting running javascript everywhere is still not in control of the computer to escape the sandbox tsai used edge reading mode immersive reader which runs under custom read address that microsoft left off the list of pages barred from running scripts from there the chain called an internal edge function meant to zip up diagnostic logs and abused it to write file with an attacker chosen name and content anywhere on disk that file write is turned into code execution in two steps the chain overwrites configuration file that controls which websites may launch which protocol handlers then restarts edge so the file is read it then launches telnet link because windows does not ship telnet program by default it searches the system path for one and runs an attacker planted copy from folder the low privileged user can write to microsoft shipped the fix on may 15 the day after the contest in edge stable version 148 3967 70 that release carried three edge specific fixes tracked as cve 2026 45492 cve 2026 45494 and cve 2026 45495 the first is recorded as security feature bypass and the second as spoofing bug both affecting edge versions before 148 3967 70 microsoft records rate the first two at on 10 point scale medium score that reflects single bug in isolation not the full chain that strings them into code execution devcore said the fix came within 24 hours of the disclosure updating edge closes this chain because the fix shipped in may browser on automatic updates has long since received it and no separate action is needed tsai built the chain by hand over about two months without any ai help and frames the work as point about where human research still matters the hard part is finding them and once you find them all chaining is the easiest part he writes of the logic bugs the research won the 2026 pwnie award for epic 30 with high memory limit that enables the memory corruption stages of the attack the custom weaponization of the php2shell exploit chain coupled with cve 2026 46300 is said to have rooted 25 servers across the japan taiwan and south korea artifacts discovered by dream indicate that the operation started with exploit development in lab environment before obtaining persistent access to government filters the servers to those located in the japan taiwan and south korea and then limits the scope to systems that match newer release branches running php 30 this step yields 240 targets the target
