title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
cleaned_text: critical 16 year old flaw in edk ii the open source code that most hardware makers use to build uefi firmware can allow an attacker to run code on machine before its operating system loads but only while the machine is booting over the network uefi firmware is the software that runs first when computer is switched on before the operating system an attacker who can reach the machine with crafted network message during such network boot can hang the boot or with work tailored to the exact firmware build run their own code before secure boot and other startup defenses load an attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way red hat and suse which both ship the affected code rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet tianocore the project behind edk ii published an advisory on october 22 and rated the flaw tracked as cve 2026 97631 out of 10 code fix exists but no stable release of edk ii contains it yet and the advisory still lists no patched version so most users have nothing to install today what the flaw lets an attacker do the flaw is buffer overflow in edk ii network boot code known as pxe during pxe boot machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from local disk as part of this the pxe driver listens for icmp error messages and the small status messages that network devices send back and copies each one into fixed 504 byte area of memory the size checks in that copy are wrong in both the ipv4 and ipv6 versions of the code so message longer than 504 bytes spills past the area and overwrites nearby memory with data the attacker chose to set this off an attacker only has to send one crafted error message to the machine address while it is in the middle of network boot no password or existing access to the machine is needed the simple result is crash the boot hangs and the machine fails to start getting code to run is much harder and far less reliable the advisory says that an attacker who knows the exact firmware build can plant counterfeit event that causes the firmware to run the attacker own code so an exploit has to be built for specific build when code runs it executes within the firmware before secure boot and other boot time checks have verified anything that timing is what makes the flaw serious code planted this way runs only once and does not survive reboot by itself that single run is still enough to install other code that does start on every boot who is affected the bug sits in edk ii up to and including edk2 stable202608 the newest stable version dated august 21 edk ii is the reference code that nearly every uefi firmware vendor builds on including the independent bios makers ami insyde and phoenix as well as microsoft hardened fork project mu the flawed copy loop has been in the code since commit added in november 2010 the hacker news found by tracing the project history pxe network boot is turned on by default in edk ii standard build the flaw does not affect home or office users who boot only from local disk it applies to organizations whose machines boot over network primarily servers and data center equipment how many shipping products carry the vulnerable code is not known intel told ars technica that none of its commercial products currently under security support are known to be affected and that it does not include the affected edk2 functionality in its reference code though an oem board vendor or system maker could add it arm said the flaw is not directly applicable to arm product portfolio both companies own firmware draws on edk ii linux distributions also ship the code red hat lists its edk2 package in red hat enterprise linux and 10 as affected and not yet fixed and suse and debian mark their equivalent packages the same way amd phoenix technologies ami microsoft and amazon did not answer the tech news site questions before publication and tianocore did not respond either so the status of their products remains unclear is there fix fix has been merged into the edk ii source code it rewrites the faulty copy so an oversized message is cut off at 504 bytes instead of spilling over and it reached the main development branch on october 15 no stable release of edk ii includes that fix yet the hacker news checked the project release tags on october 28 and found the newest edk2 stable202608 predates it and the advisory still lists the patched version as not patched currently microsoft project mu has already pulled the fix into its release branches and cut tagged builds on october 26 even with the fix public in source server operator has nothing to install until the maker of their firmware ships bios or uefi update built from it that step is at least straightforward jesse michael principal researcher at the firmware security firm eclypsium told ars technica unlike secure boot bypasses such as boothole and blacklotus the flaw can be fixed with basic code fix and does not require certificate or key revocations until that update arrives the advisory lists no workaround because the flaw can only be reached during network boot operators who do not need pxe can disable it to reduce exposure ars also advised watching boot time network traffic and logs for signs of attempts how it became public the flaw was found by alex matrosov of anthropic and dan holmes mitra of google the advisory credits coordinated disclosure had been planned for january 2027 that plan was overtaken on september 28 when pull request to edk ii signed off by an ami engineer publicly described the flaw by its cve number and included the fix once the people who found it saw the post tianocore published its advisory on october 22 weeks before the planned date with the patch public ars noted that skilled attackers can study it to determine how the flaw is triggered and build working exploits there is no sign the flaw has been used in an attack it was not in cisa known exploited vulnerabilities catalog as of its october 27 update and no researcher has reported seeing it exploited the flaw is also not on its own way into network ars technica reported after putting questions to several firmware researchers the realistic attacker is an insider or someone who has already gained low level foothold on the local network and wants to dig deeper an attacker intent on compromising nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components like the endpoint tpm said hd moore the creator of metasploit and chief research officer at the security firm dragos in comments to ars technica this could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short term network access and it would be even easier in theft scenario it is not the first serious flaw in edk ii network boot code in january 2024 researchers disclosed pixiefail set of nine flaws in the same part of edk ii also reachable during pxe boot ars reported that fuzzing projects started after pixiefail to find more bugs in the code did not catch this one found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

demand the reward program opened on october 28 and pays only if tip helps lead to an arrest or an international wanted notice the service hosts windows desktops used for fx trading and broker has linked unauthorized trades on some of its customers accounts to logins leaked from the service gmo says the attackers took customer information it received demand for about 50 million about billion on october 21 from people it believes carried out the attack they have also threatened its customers trading accounts and data on october 27 the attackers posted material on their website that they say is information about gmo and its customers the site domain including its mirror sites was shut down at about japan time on october 28 and gmo plans to act against any new site how the reward works gmo internet group runs and pays for the program called gmo cybercrime bounty tips are sent by email to an address listed on dedicated website in japanese english or chinese and can be anonymous the program is open until an arrest an international wanted notice or october 27 2027 whichever comes first gmo wants information linking people servers domains ip addresses accounts or cryptocurrency addresses to the attack extortion or movement of money along with evidence of how the crimes were carried out guesses unsupported accusations and reposts of public information generally do not qualify tip earns money only if it leads to an arrest including one by police outside japan or to an international wanted notice such as an interpol red notice gmo decides how much each tip helped and one tipster can receive the full million or the total can be split tipsters must prove their identity before payment and if no tip qualifies no payment is made some people cannot be paid including anyone involved in the crime anyone who got information illegally such as by buying leaked data and gmo staff gmo tells tipsters not to break into systems negotiate with or pay the attackers or send leaked data credentials or malware tips are shared with police and other authorities in japan and abroad as needed gmo has already given police all its evidence on the threats including communication records gmo will never ask tipsters for passwords authentication codes or fees and it writes to them only from addresses ending in cybercrimebounty gmo the breach and the trading accounts gmo internet the subsidiary that runs the service found on october 20 that third party had installed malicious programs on some customers servers it shut down the servers on every plan from october 21 it counts 26 739 servers as potentially affected which is not the number of confirmed break ins or data thefts on october 24 gmo said it had confirmed security problem in the service systems unauthorized access to the service and the exfiltration of customer information from the company anything customers stored on the servers may have been viewed including login credentials saved in trading software such as metatrader and mt4 mt5 gmo does not keep customers payment card data on the servers customers began reporting trades they did not recognize on october 21 broker oanda japan has confirmed that third party logged in to and traded on some of its customers accounts using id and password pairs it believes were leaked from the gmo servers it has restricted trading on accounts that may be affected and as of october 26 it had not found break in or leak in its own core systems another broker fxtf warned on october 22 that third parties may have stolen the logins of some customers who use vps servers in an attack it believes hit another company vps servers they may also have used the logins to log in and trade it told customers who had connected to desktop cloud to change their fxtf passwords from device that had never connected to it gmo internet group said in stock exchange filing on october 28 that it had not yet confirmed how many customers its payments will cover how much information was published or which trades qualify for compensation it had not confirmed any impact from the breach on its other services the threats and the leak gmo says the attackers threatened to keep manipulating customers accounts at more than 70 securities and fx firms to publish information about the service and about customers pcs to hit those pcs with ransomware and to publish details of gmo systems they set noon on october 27 for publishing customer information and launching the ransomware attack no ransomware attack had been confirmed as of 55 japan time that day the material posted on october 27 was what the attackers called one customer personal information itmedia news reported that afternoon gmo was checking it that day the attackers collected information about anyone who visited their site according to gmo which tells visitors to run full antivirus scan it asks people not to visit the site or any new one and not to repost or link to the material how the attackers got in as of october 28 gmo had not said how the attackers got in masatoshi kumagai who heads gmo internet group wrote in an october 25 blog post that the group own white hat hackers had warned the team running the service about problems in advance the response was neither fast nor thorough enough he wrote and the attackers took advantage of the gap on their website the attackers claimed that one administrator account was shared across all the servers and that customers pc drives were visible from the servers by default when they connected itmedia news reported they also claimed they used flaw in the service to reach customers own pcs gmo had not publicly confirmed these claims either by october 26 gmo had collected pcs from customers who offered them for analysis as of 11 59 japan time on october 27 it had found no malware including ransomware on the pcs it had finished checking that does not confirm that every customer device is safe and the analysis is still ongoing what customers should do gmo has told desktop cloud customers to take these steps change trading account and trading software passwords from device not used for fx trading such as phone end every logged in session through the broker if needed even after changing the password check trading history and balances and report unrecognized trades to the broker first turn on two factor authentication where the broker offers it change passwords reused on other services or saved in the browser run full antivirus scan on devices used to connect and back up data do not reply to messages from anyone claiming to be behind the attack or open their links or files ignore offers to recover lost money for fee gmo will never ask for password or authentication code gmo internet will pay every current user 000 and cover actual trading losses and fees from trades it confirms were unauthorized and caused by the breach customers whose information it confirms was published will also get 10 000 to 25 000 for each type of information exposed gmo will not restart the service on the breached systems as they are customers who want windows desktop will be offered move to separate service free for six months and only with their consent with details due by october 30 found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
cleaned_text: tailscale has released version 104 to fix flaws in its built in ssh server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch the flaws are in how tailscale ssh forwards network connections job the tailscale background process carries out with root privileges to use them an attacker must already control device that the network access rules permit to open an ssh session to the target with forwarding allowed in that rule the flaws come from report called tailworm published days before the fix by erica windisch of cyberdione labs who tested released versions of the tailscale client and the self hosted headscale control server in lab tailscale ssh decides who can connect using device identity and the network policy file not password or key so an attacker does not need stolen credentials only foothold on device the policy already trusts the flaws don allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary tailscale ssh servers tailscale said and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows tailscale ssh server runs only on linux and the open source macos build the attacker own device can be any platform the problem is in socket forwarding when permitted ssh session forwarded connection to unix socket on the server the tailscale process checked the path but then operated as root timing trick let an attacker swap in different path after that check defeating the safeguard meant to limit which sockets forwarding could reach in windisch own tests forwarding to the docker control socket produced root shell and read the system password file etc shadow with no administrator rights tailscale bulletin describes the reach more narrowly saying an attacker could get to root only sockets such as the docker socket or the tailscaled local api in 104 tailscale changed the server to carry out forwarding as the logged in user rather than as root and to rely on the operating system own file permissions in place of its earlier path check the release covers security bulletins ts 2026 014 the ssh socket forwarding flaws above which let permitted session reach root only sockets such as the docker socket or the tailscaled local api ts 2026 015 way for permitted ssh session to use up server memory and crash the tailscale process cutting all tailscale networking on that node ts 2026 016 flaw in tailscale serve where forward to unix socket could reach the tailscaled local api giving remote control of the node plus related socket swap issue ts 2026 017 flaw where with tls serve and or more mounts one request could receive another mount permission headers what to do users of tailscale ssh should update to version 104 or later if you cannot update server yet you can turn off ssh forwarding on it by setting ts ssh disable forwarding in the tailscaled service environment and restarting the service which tailscale says turns off forwarding without disabling tailscale ssh and blocks several of the more serious findings tailscale also recommends reviewing ssh access rules so that only the users and devices that need access have it tailscale suggests using ssh check mode which requires user to sign in again before session starts for sensitive systems check mode does not stop these forwarding flaws it guards the start of session whereas the forwarding occurs within session that has already been approved if server may already have been compromised windisch report says the fix alone is not enough stolen device key stays valid until the device is deleted at the control plane because reimaging the machine does not revoke it tailscale notices do not cover this case the picture is worse on headscale the self hosted control server on headscale ssh forwarding is granted on every accepted session and cannot be turned off in the policy so windisch report says every ssh grant there should be treated as giving root the newest headscale release version 29 from october 13 does not fix the reported issues is it worm windisch called the chain wormable in her tests one compromised device could spread to every device the policy allowed with no passwords no stolen keys and no user action in under second per step two controls stopped the spread in those tests writing access rules as single device to device pairs held it back and binding device keys to hardware such as tpm kept stolen identity from being reused elsewhere tailscale rejected the worm description the findings do not describe self replicating malware that spreads between machines on its own the company said but lateral movement limited to the connections policy file already allows it called the privilege escalation problems serious security issues said it had reproduced the main ones and added that it is still working out which configurations are affected disclosure and earlier fixes as of publication the bulletins carry no cve identifiers or severity scores and none state the oldest affected version the report also covered tailscale app connectors and its serve and funnel features tailscale said the app connector finding is in conn25 an experimental feature it has not released and that the connectors customers use today are not affected of serve and funnel findings it fixed and said the other work as designed windisch published the report without coordinating the release with tailscale first which she has described as reported but not coordinated tailscale said it received the report on the morning of saturday october 24 about hours before windisch published it and that its engineers were already looking at the same parts of the code neither tailscale nor the report says the flaws have been used in real attacks the proof of concept code is not public and windisch said she gave it only to tailscale security team the report is the latest in run of fixes in the same part of tailscale this year in june tailscale fixed separate flaw in tailscale ssh unix socket forwarding that let an unprivileged user reach privileged socket in version 98 found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
cleaned_text: the critical oracle peoplesoft bug that shinyhunters has exploited since may is not one flaw but three chained together the researchers who reported it said this week oracle patched all three under single identifier cve 2026 35273 in june its root is server side request forgery ssrf that reaches an internal management interface because peoplesoft trusts its own loopback address by default opening the door to remote code execution without login the breakdown comes from bobby gould of the zero day initiative zdi whose team reported the flaw to oracle in its analysis zdi said it reported three distinct vulnerabilities across two peoplesoft components and that it is working with oracle to assign separate cve to each as of this week the one june identifier is still the only one on the record cve 2026 35273 affects peoplesoft enterprise peopletools versions 61 and 62 carries cvss score of and lets an unauthenticated attacker take over the server over the network oracle released its fix in an out of band security alert on june 10 the flaw is on cisa known exploited vulnerabilities catalog attackers were already using it before that fix was in place mandiant and google threat intelligence group gtig attribute campaign to the group it tracks as unc6240 better known as shinyhunters that exploited the flaw between may 27 and june mostly against universities because that activity came before oracle june 10 advisory it was zero day the whole time in september follow up mandiant reported renewed larger wave that spread beyond education to technology it services healthcare agriculture transport and government affecting dozens of systems worldwide zdi analysis explains what that single patch actually closed two peoplesoft components are involved both run as separate web applications the integration gateway psigw exchanges messages with outside systems the environment management hub psemhub is an internal admin interface that is supposed to answer only to trusted hosts the first flaw is the ssrf in psigw an attacker sends request to its listening connector and controls both the address it forwards to and the full payload it sends zdi said the handler does no check that the destination is legitimate target that alone would be limited except for what it can reach psemhub decides who to trust by checking the requester against list in file named allowedhosts properties that file ships with the local loopback address 127 already on the list so an attacker points the ssrf at 127 the request arrives looking like it came from the machine itself and the trust check passes the internal interface oracle meant to wall off is now reachable from outside from there zdi described two ways to turn that access into code execution one abuses psemhub command meant to write log entries the caller controls both the file contents and the exact path on disk so an attacker writes web shell into the application directory and runs commands as the peoplesoft service account the other writes malicious xml file that psemhub reads using java xmldecoder when the service next starts thereby running the attacker code without planting web shell at all the second path leaves less for standard detection to catch the design decision at the center zdi said is that allowing loopback access by default makes the trust check ineffective once the ssrf exists that matters for defenders who thought firewall rule had covered them in the september wave mandiant found shinyhunters slipping past web application firewall waf rules that blocked the psemhub path by url encoding single character requesting 50semhub instead many waf rules match the path plain text while the peoplesoft server decodes it and serves the page what to do the fix and the guidance here come from oracle and mandiant not from zdi analysis which covers the flaw rather than the response apply the patch install oracle security alert fix for cve 2026 35273 and stay on supported peopletools release mandiant is explicit that path based waf blocking is not substitute for patching if you cannot patch yet disable the environment management hub service in multi server setups or remove the psemhub application in single server setups as oracle alert advises restricting these admin endpoints does not break normal user sessions if you may already be hit mandiant recommends treating any host with web shell as compromised preserving evidence and rotating every credential reachable from the peoplesoft tier shinyhunters steals data and then demands payment so affected organizations should prepare for extortion one thing the sources do not settle is whether applying the patch removes access an attacker already gained oracle alert does not address it and mandiant guidance to rotate credentials and hunt for web shells assumes it does not patching closes the door it does not by itself evict someone already inside found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Adobe Commerce PolyShell Attacks Breach Hundreds of Stores as Brotli Exploit Traffic Emerges
cleaned_text: the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency cisa on tuesday added two vulnerabilities impacting adobe commerce and magento and google brotli decoder library to its known exploited vulnerabilities kev catalog citing evidence of active exploitation the vulnerabilities are listed below cve 2026 111497 cvss score an unchecked return value vulnerability in google brotli that could allow remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory disclose sensitive memory contents cause denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code using crafted brotli compressed stream cve 2026 48356 cvss score an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in adobe commerce and magento that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim account or session the development comes days after sansec said it observed attackers leveraging cve 2026 48356 also known as polyshell to breach hundreds of commerce stores to inject malicious loader via magento cms block the loader is designed to fetch and execute an attacker controlled payload although no next stage malware has been recovered to date making it challenging to determine what the exact goals of the campaign are the activity is assessed to be ongoing since at least july 2025 as for cve 2026 111497 aka broccoli2shell http2shell and node2shell telemetry data from threat intelligence firm previdian shows that one exploitation attempt has been recorded against its honeypot sensors from based ip address as of october 27 2026 it currently not known if these efforts are broad in scope an attacker who can supply brotli data that an application decompresses with node zlib can corrupt process memory rapid7 said according to node js this corruption can lead to process crash disclosure of sensitive process memory or remote code execution exposure therefore depends on whether an application passes attacker controlled compressed data to the affected decoder ellio also reported on monday that its sensors have recorded cve 2026 111497 exploit traffic in the wild carrying the public exploit that we confirmed gets shell on vulnerable builds the activity originates from 94 154 43 an ip address geolocated to the netherlands that has also engaged in exploitation efforts targeting php2shell two critical flaws in php that could result in unauthenticated remote code execution the attacker payload is genuine correctly structured node2shell exploitation attempt for node v24 22 the brotli stream staged displacement pivot pair and delivery are all correct and identical to the public tooling ellio said this is indicative of the rce being adopted by an operator focused on mass exploitation the fact that brotli is widely distributed open source library and adopted by numerous projects has provoked an emergency response prompting various vendors to release patches or assess if their products are affected by the flaw this includes php which has shipped versions 12 27 36 and 35 as well as node js bun envoy proxy istio net python clickhouse the php brotli extension and the ruby brotli gem links to some of the advisories are below amazon linux broadcom bun cisco cloudflare cloudlinux envoy proxy f5 fortinet imperva istio microsoft azure microsoft net node js palo alto networks php qualys red hat safe security strapi tanium tenable ubuntu upwind node js fixed the vulnerability in versions 22 23 24 22 and 26 12 akamai said the node js advisory does not offer workaround so upgrading is the only complete remediation organizations running discontinued release line should move to supported release line google owned wiz has warned that 91 of cloud environments have resources vulnerable to cve 2026 111497 and 82 of cloud environments have publicly exposed node js instances node2shell is not bug in every node js service but bug in services that decode attacker influenced brotli sysdig said express with default json parsing puts large number of instances of them in that group the demonstrated impact thus far is crashes at scale and code execution in narrow configuration so patch order should follow reachability federal civilian executive branch fceb agencies have time until november 10 2026 to apply the necessary fixes against the two flaws found title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
cleaned_text: flaw in the linux kernel tcp code tracked as cve 2026 98432 affects ubuntu red hat enterprise linux rhel and other linux distributions the kernel own cve team rates it out of 10 on the cvss scale anthropic said on october 27 that its ai model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on linux servers with multipath tcp listener as of october 29 ubuntu and rhel have not released fixed kernel red hat amazon oracle and suse score the flaw between and lower than the kernel team the flaw is race condition in the code that sets up new ipv4 tcp connections it can make the kernel read memory it has already freed bug type known as use after free the kernel fix credits anthropic researcher xinyang ge with reporting the bug neither the cve record nor the fix mentions multipath tcp mptcp the link between that feature and this bug comes from anthropic post mptcp lets one connection use several network paths at once on linux an application must request mptcp when it opens socket as of go 24 go programs do so by default for the sockets they listen on the go security team said on october 29 anthropic post says the flaw was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches for distribution users that fix arrives only in the vendor kernel package debian oracle linux suse and amazon linux have shipped fixed packages at least for some of their kernels but ubuntu and rhel have not which distributions have fix distribution vendor rating status as of october 29 fixed package or advisory ubuntu 22 04 lts 24 04 lts 26 04 lts and 26 10 priority high work in progress none released ubuntu 16 04 18 04 and 20 04 priority high vulnerable none released rhel and 10 openshift moderate cve page important advisory file affected none released rhel not applicable not affected not needed amazon linux 2023 kernel6 18 package important fixed october 24 kernel6 18 18 56 125 164 amzn2023 alas2023 2026 3251 amazon linux 2023 kernel6 12 package important fixed october 29 in amazon advisory amazon cve page still says pending kernel6 12 12 113 138 209 amzn2023 alas2023 2026 3335 amazon linux amazon linux 2023 kernel package important pending fix none released oracle linux and 10 uek kernel important fixed october 16 elsa 2026 500397 elsa 2026 500398 elsa 2026 500399 debian trixie stable no score listed fixed october 16 linux 12 113 dsa 6568 debian 12 bookworm no score listed fixed october 17 and october 22 linux 190 dla 4841 linux 12 12 113 deb12u1 dla 4850 suse linux micro opensuse leap 16 important fixed kernel default 12 160000 40 or later sles 15 sp4 to sp6 ltss sles 16 sle micro to important in testing none released sles 15 sp7 important affected fix in progress none released ubuntu also lists its cloud fips and real time kernels as vulnerable or as work in progress on october 29 red hat said its fixes were currently deferred to future update by october 30 it listed rhel and 10 and openshift as affected rather than fix deferred neither red hat nor ubuntu gives release date how the bug works the race happens during the tcp handshake when connection is completed the kernel hands the ip options stored with the pending request to the new socket without copying them if that socket is destroyed while another cpu is still using the options to answer resent connection request the kernel reads freed memory ipv6 is not affected by this race because the kernel copies the options for ipv6 connections the bug was introduced in linux kernel developers applied fix on october ten days before the cve was published the fix makes the kernel wait until other cpus finish reading the options before it frees them why the scores differ the kernel cve team added the score to the cve record on october 24 nine days after publishing the cve its score assumes an attacker who sends tcp connection request carrying ipv4 record route or timestamp options then resends the request to try to win the race the team rated attack complexity low saying both sides of the race are attacker induced in that case the team says the bug could send nearby kernel memory back to the attacker corrupt kernel memory or crash the system as of october 28 the national vulnerability database nvd had not added its own score and showed the kernel team ubuntu page also shows that score red hat cve page rates the flaw moderate scoring it because the race is hard to win it says the most likely result is kernel crash with memory corruption possible in theory and that no confidentiality or integrity impact has been demonstrated red hat machine readable advisory file updated on october 29 lists the impact as important and scores the flaw with high confidentiality and integrity impact red hat bug tracker changed the issue severity from medium to high the same day on that day the cve page showed moderate and oracle and suse also score the flaw with the same cvss vector as red hat advisory file those scores match the kernel team on every metric except attack complexity which the vendors rate high and the kernel team rates low amazon scores it what anthropic says it built anthropic described the linux exploit in an october 27 post about flaws that its ai model claude found and exploited the hacker news covered the post on october 28 claude wrote the exploit after initial prompting anthropic said the exploit works in two stages first the race makes the kernel send extra bytes back to the attacker once one of those replies contains kernel address the attacker can get around kaslr the kernel memory address randomization second the same bug overflows buffer and overwrites callback pointer with the address of payload the attacker had already placed in kernel memory when the kernel calls that pointer the payload executes shell command of the attacker choice as root lost race only fails that one connection attempt and does not crash the system so an attacker can keep trying the company said in its test leaking kernel address took 48 minutes and reaching command execution took more minutes the post does not include the exploit code the kernel version or the configuration anthropic tested red hat says remote attacker who can reach an exposed tcp service could trigger the race anthropic root exploit however targeted servers with multipath tcp listener the post does not say whether servers without one can be taken over the same way as of october 29 none of the vendor advisories the cve record or anthropic post reports attacks using the flaw it does not appear in copy of cisa known exploited vulnerabilities catalog that luxembourg circl last updated on october 28 what to do now where your distribution has released fixed kernel install it the table above lists the packages and advisories for debian oracle linux suse and amazon linux if you build your own kernel the fix is in linux 10 272 15 223 190 159 12 113 18 56 10 and the kernel cve team recommends updating to the latest stable kernel it says the kernel community does not support cherry picking individual fixes ubuntu rhel and some amazon linux and suse releases have no fixed kernel to install yet red hat says no available mitigation meets its standards for being easy to deploy suitable for most installations and stable none of the other distributions advisories lists one the distributions advisories and anthropic post do not say whether turning off multipath tcp in the kernel or blocking incoming connection requests that carry ip options would lower the risk for go programs the go security team says setting godebug multipathtcp in program environment disables mptcp by default at runtime adding godebug multipathtcp to the main module go mod file does the same at build time but code that calls setmultipathtcp overrides both the team calls turning off mptcp program by program fragile mitigation single mptcp listener left exposed still leaves system vulnerable and the approach assumes every working exploit depends on mptcp the team also says the underlying bug is not specific to mptcp that systems with no mptcp listeners may be vulnerable to similar attacks and that the best fix is to upgrade to patched kernel the story was updated on october 30 to add the go security team guidance for go programs and to reflect that red hat now lists rhel and 10 and openshift as affected rather than fix deferred found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive title: Fake ChatGPT and Claude Apps Abuse Signed Executables to Deploy Crypto Miners
cleaned_text: threat actors are delivering malicious loaders and cryptocurrency miners under the guise of artificial intelligence ai desktop applications for anthropic claude and openai chatgpt as part of campaign dubbed yoba the activity involves creating fake github projects that claim to be desktop applications like gpt sol gpt astra and claude opus only to deliver malware family called yobaloader the malware is placed next to legitimate signed executables from openai and anthropic so it can be loaded indirectly technique commonly known as dll sideloading which is often used to bypass security protections check point research said in an analysis to add to the project credibility the attackers set up github io pages to describe the capabilities of the software although the github projects popularity is not manipulated using techniques like ghost networks signs point to the use of seo poisoning tactics to ensure that links to them are surfaced on top of search results on google some of the identified github pages links are below github com gpt sol free desktop gpt github io github com gpt gpt github io github com gpt astra gpt astra github io gpt astra github io github com opus opus github io opus github io each repository uses different email address edwardcarlsonmkym outlook com daxschneiderdjuu outlook com and rioprestonlfyx outlook com and the uploader appears to operate in utc utc and utc respectively check point said this inconsistency likely reflects deliberate attempt to obscure the threat actor true operational time zone hosted within these repositories are zip archives that among other files contain two specific components setup exe legitimate signed openai codex or claude executable winmm dll malicious dll that sideloaded by the executable the dll is dropper codenamed yobadropper which implements checksum value checks by hashing the basename of its host executable and if it matches hard coded value 0xe6c2f326 in other words the check requires it to be launched under setup exe and fails if the dll is executed on its own inside sandboxed environment additional anti analysis techniques and pre checks include 200 000 iterations of sleep 5500 which amounts to 12 73 days and skipping machines whose keyboard layout corresponds to that of russia belarus tajikistan armenia azerbaijan georgia kazakhstan kyrgyzstan turkmenistan and uzbekistan another language id excluded from the infection process is tatar notably missing from the list is ukraine which used to be historically included in such checks yobadropper for its part triggers dll sideloading chain of its own comprising wmpdmc exe and ampdui dll copying the former from its system32 folder and placing it in new directory named wmprocess created under programdata the dropper then extracts and decrypts an embedded payload and drops it into the same folder as wmpdui dll it also establishes persistence by means of scheduled task that launches the legitimate executable to load the malicious payload the second dll is yobaloader it implements the same anti sandbox technique as yobadropper requiring the malware to be run only by wmpdmc exe by checking the hash against hard coded value 0x552751e3 the loader is responsible for three main tasks downloads an image from telegram channel me yoba fanclub uses the last 50 bytes as seed to generate domain based on three lists of dictionary words and an integer value in the range 999 using domain generation algorithm dga the end result is domain in the format adjective noun verb digit dedyn io queries google dns over https doh api to obtain base64 encoded command from dns txt record by passing the constructed domain as input decrypts the response to obtain the link to fetch the next stage payload files catbox moe z5zpy9 dat by relying on doh service and common file hosting platforms the actor aims to bypass passive dns monitoring and some gateway based security protections making their command and control traffic harder to distinguish from regular user activity check point said the downloaded payload is then injected into svchost exe resulting in the execution of an xmrig cryptocurrency miner evidence indicates that the first github repository was created around july 2026 although the malicious releases were not uploaded until the end of august what more early versions of yobaloader have been found to only exclude russia from infection while also incorporating extensive anti debugging and anti vm checks which have since been removed in newer versions the yoba campaign shows how attackers can use trusted platforms and the current interest in ai tools to distribute malware in way that looks believable and harmless at first glance check point said by packaging their code together with well known software names and hosting it on github they lower the chances that users or basic security checks will immediately flag the files as suspicious found title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Leads Benchmarks for Finding, Exploiting, and Patching Vulnerabilities
cleaned_text: google on wednesday took the wraps off gemini carbon its latest frontier model with state of the art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities it shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense landing firm lead in sec bench pro 88 for finding vulnerabilities exploitgym 54 for exploitation and cwe bench 71 for patching koray kavukcuoglu senior vice president of google deepmind and chief ai architect at google said on the artificial analysis intelligence index benchmark carbon leads with score of 59 surpassing anthropic claude opus 58 openai gpt astra 57 gpt sol 55 one of the core focus areas is cybersecurity where the latest iteration reportedly delivers significant performance improvements across the board including vulnerability detection validation and remediation carbon is also twice as likely to generate secure code versus argon google also emphasized that carbon attempts to respond to complex or high pressure tasks by seeking human input in the face of ambiguity rather than guessing or forcing path forward as well as resisting every evaluated attack attempt at indirect prompt injection the debut of gemini carbon comes less than week after the tech giant unveiled gemini argon the release plan is similar to that of its predecessor with the rollout currently limited to subset of cyber defenders before expanding access to other trusted partners as part of its fairwind program google also said it actively engaged in the government voluntary process for pre release model testing the development comes as openai released gpt terra which it described as fast efficient model that excels at communication and computer based tasks gpt terra meets the critical threshold in cybersecurity under our preparedness framework and maintains the protections developed for gpt astra openai said gpt terra brings with it the alignment improvements of the gpt series according to our evaluations gpt terra is more likely to stay within scope and honestly disclose limitations and potential blockers to the user compared to gpt terra in our prompt injection tests gpt terra also showed strong resistance to malicious instructions designed to divert it from the user task earlier this week rival anthropic also disclosed that an unreleased internal research model uncovered critical title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
cleaned_text: flaw in telegram for android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of victim phone through voice call once the victim answered according to security startup nebusec the attacker needed only an ordinary telegram account telegram fixed the flaw in version 12 10 of the app released in late september and nebusec disclosed it on october 29 combined with an information leak bug the flaw gives the attacker an escape from the telegram app to android nebusec co founder and chief executive eten zou told the hacker news adding an android root exploit then gives full control of the phone including its messages microphone and camera the flaw can be triggered in every version from through 12 10 zou said those versions came out between march 2022 and september 2026 the company confirmed it in private voice calls on arm64 based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects telegram ios and desktop apps or group calls anyone using telegram for android should make sure the app is on version 12 10 or later the version number appears at the bottom of the app settings page the flaw had no cve identifier as of october 29 the attack needs the victim to be called and to answer zou said so setting telegram call privacy option to nobody blocks it and so does declining the call nebusec has not seen the flaw used in real attacks and believes no one else had realized it could be turned into remote code execution nebusec reported the flaw to telegram on september 26 after version 12 10 had shipped telegram acknowledged the report but did not believe the flaw could be turned into remote code execution so no cve was assigned and no bug bounty was paid zou said the hacker news has asked telegram for comment during telegram call the two apps send each other short messages to set up the call and report its state one type called mediastate reports whether the microphone is muted whether the camera is on and how the video is rotated the flaw was in the code that reads mediastate messages that code did not handle missing fields correctly and accessed memory it should not according to nebusec telegram published source code for version 12 10 contains flaw that matches that description review by the hacker news found when mediastate message included rotation value the code checked that value it then read different field the video state even if the message had no such field version 12 10 reads the rotation value from the right field the calling code that uses this message was switched on in version the first version nebusec names telegram android ios and desktop apps use one shared library called tgcalls for calls change labeled fix camera rotation made the same correction in tgcalls on april 21 2026 telegram ios source code included that change from version 12 released in may and the desktop app code from version released in july telegram for android received it in version 12 10 in september whether the earlier code could be exploited in those apps has not been shown nebusec video shows two phones one marked as the attacker and one as the victim the victim accepts telegram call about half minute into the call the victim phone switches to its home screen the app icons fall down the screen and hacked by nebusec logo appears the video does not show which telegram or android version the victim phone was running no combinator says its code security product which runs on openai gpt model found the flaw in july the company described an android exploit chain that started with firefox flaw and reached the kernel of stickers the flaw tracked as cve 2026 111105 cvss score can let an attacker run code if user opens malicious file or page zdi said telegram had told zdi in march that checks on its servers mitigated title: The Rise of the Threat Operator: How AI Will Redefine Security Operations and Careers
cleaned_text: ai is beginning to take over much of the work that has traditionally defined the security analyst job investigating alerts collecting evidence correlating activity across tools and executing response actions are becoming tasks that ai systems can perform on their own as these capabilities mature security operations centers socs will see major changes in how work is organized how decisions are made and what is expected of the people responsible for defending organizations for security professionals this is chance to take on much broader role as ai assumes more of the operational workload analysts can move beyond individual alerts and investigations to direct the defense across the entire security lifecycle we call this emerging role the threat operator an ai native security professional who translates business risk into defensive priorities directs ai driven operations and exercises judgment over the decisions and actions taken by those systems the impact reaches beyond day to day soc work it will change the skills organizations need how security professionals develop expertise and the career paths open to people entering the field from individual tasks to overall defense the traditional soc developed around specialized functions each supported by its own tools and workflows threat intelligence teams study adversaries detection engineers create rules threat hunters search for activity that existing controls may have missed analysts investigate alerts and incident responders contain confirmed threats these functions are closely related yet the work often moves between teams through separate systems tickets and manual handoffs ai is starting to tie these activities together for example intelligence about new threat can lead to hunting hypothesis which can reveal detection gap and produce new detection that detection may identify suspicious activity requiring investigation followed by containment and further improvements to the organization defenses ai agents can coordinate and execute these workflows carrying context and findings from one stage to the next that changes where security professionals add the most value threat operator works across the defensive lifecycle setting priorities based on the organization exposure business operations and threat landscape they determine which risks deserve attention what the defense should accomplish how much autonomy ai should have and when decision requires human intervention they are also responsible for judging whether the operation is actually improving security consider financial institution facing newly identified threat targeting identity infrastructure ai agents could assess the institution exposure hunt for relevant activity identify gaps in existing detections and recommend defensive actions the threat operator would provide the institutional context needed to guide that work including which systems support critical business processes what constitutes unacceptable risk and which actions require authorization the result is gradual shift from human in the loop to human on the loop with security professionals supervising and governing ai driven operations the level of autonomy will depend on the maturity of the technology the consequences of particular actions and the organization tolerance for risk but human remains accountable throughout rethinking how security professionals gain experience junior security analysts will feel some of the biggest effects for decades the soc has provided an entry point into cybersecurity with analysts developing their skills through alert triage evidence collection investigations documentation and escalation although much of this work is repetitive it has also served as an apprenticeship over time analysts learn how systems behave how attackers operate and how experienced practitioners distinguish genuine threats from benign activity as ai absorbs more of these responsibilities organizations will need to rethink how that experience is acquired the traditional progression from handling simple alerts to managing complex investigations may become less relevant as ai takes on more sophisticated work without deliberate approach to training security teams may struggle to develop the experienced professionals they will need in the future ai can also open up different path for professional development junior threat operators can gain supervised exposure to much wider range of security activities examining how intelligence informs hunting how detections are developed how investigations reach conclusions and how response decisions affect the business they can review the evidence behind ai generated findings challenge assumptions identify missing context and learn from the decisions made by more experienced colleagues this only works if organizations invest in technical fundamentals and structured mentorship analysts still need to understand networks operating systems attacker techniques and the security technologies underlying ai driven workflows experienced practitioners will need to teach younger colleagues how to evaluate conclusions recognize uncertainty and exercise judgment when the available evidence is incomplete the skills needed for the current generation of security analysts technical proficiency has often been measured through familiarity with security tools and the ability to extract useful information from them query languages detection logic endpoint telemetry and investigation techniques have been central to the profession those skills still matter ai adds new demands on top of them orchestration governance and interpreting automated decisions threat operators will need to translate business security risks into clear defensive objectives that ai systems can execute they must understand the organization architecture critical assets operational dependencies and relevant adversaries and know how to communicate that context to ai agents their work will involve evaluating hypotheses validating evidence setting escalation criteria and determining whether an automated action has achieved its intended outcome for example an ai system investigating compromised server may recommend immediate isolation that call could be technically sound but the server may support critical business process where disruption carries significant consequences threat operator must understand those dependencies and determine how the response should proceed balancing containment requirements with operational risk this need for defined oversight and accountability is also reflected in the nist ai risk management framework the role will combine four areas of expertise business security risk understanding organizational priorities critical assets and the consequences of security decisions threat and adversary understanding interpreting intelligence and anticipating how attackers may target the environment defensive operations understanding detection hunting investigation and response across the security lifecycle ai orchestration and judgment directing ai workflows evaluating their conclusions and governing automated actions building career path around defensive outcomes the threat operator role should become career path with increasing levels of responsibility early career operators can focus on validating evidence reviewing ai conclusions adding environmental context and understanding how decisions connect across the defensive lifecycle as they gain experience they can begin translating business risks into defensive objectives directing agent workflows identifying coverage gaps and determining when operations should escalate or act senior threat operators will take responsibility for defining autonomy boundaries governing consequential actions evaluating the reliability of ai driven decisions and measuring whether security operations are reducing organizational risk professionals may enter this career path from investigations threat intelligence detection engineering incident response security architecture or risk management bringing different areas of expertise to role that spans the entire defensive operation security leaders should start building the training governance and progression frameworks needed to support these responsibilities that includes establishing which decisions require human approval how operators validate ai generated evidence how autonomy expands as systems demonstrate reliability and how individual performance is evaluated measures such as the quality of defensive decisions the closure of detection gaps and improvements in threat coverage will matter more alongside traditional operational metrics this will happen at different speeds in different organizations security professionals will have more say in how their organizations defend themselves the old soc trained people to operate tools the ai native soc has to train them to operate the defense conifers ai cognitivesoc platform uses agentic ai to connect threat intelligence hunting detection engineering investigation and response and every agent action comes with reasoning chain and evidence trail that analysts can review learn more about how conifers helps security teams direct and govern ai driven defense across the full soc lifecycle found title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
cleaned_text: github has announced that it introducing new package firewall as preview to block installation of suspicious npm packages during installation time the firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity acting as an install time policy gate github said the feature which currently supports only npm packages is available in public preview for all github enterprise cloud customers including data resident github enterprise cloud according to the microsoft subsidiary the firewall is placed between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories so as to deter malware attacks that compromise systems when packages are installed this behavior can expose users to severe security risks especially when artificial intelligence ai agents and ci runners automatically install dependencies to complete task or build without their explicit permission the idea is that endpoints like coding agents and ci cd hosts use the firewall for their requests instead of directly pointing to the public package registries the firewall then checks package downloads against policy controls such as minimum package age and malware advisories and blocks downloads that do not meet those policies to use the firewall administrators are required to configure policy controls such as the ones listed below block known malware by checking against the github advisory database for active malware advisories block packages based on the severity of vulnerabilities by checking the github advisory database for flaws that affect the requested package version the control defaults to critical only as the severity level that blocks an installation although users can choose high or higher medium or higher or any severity block attestation downgrades by comparing attestations for the requested package version with those of earlier versions and stop the download if the requested version does not have an slsa attestation block newly introduced install scripts by checking whether the package recently added scripts that run using preinstall or postinstall hooks which can be abused to steal sensitive data block packages based on cooldown period that prevents versions that are newer than the configured minimum age from being installed the value can range from to 365 days the default value is day users can disable it by setting it to block packages based on cooldown period that prevents versions that are newer than the configured minimum age from being installed the value can range from to 365 days the default value is day users can disable it by setting it to users who need access to package that gets blocked erroneously by the firewall can submit an exception request which can then be approved by enterprise administrators and security managers the development comes as rust 100 which is scheduled for release on november 12 2026 readies to add support for configurable minimum publish age allowing security scanners and maintainers time to flag and block malicious crate releases before they can be installed or used by users the value defined via the global min publish age option in cargo config toml allows users to specify minimum publication age in days or weeks if left unspecified seven day waiting period is applied by default to skip releases published within that window over the past year similar waiting periods have been implemented across open source ecosystems including npm python microsoft visual studio code ruby bun pnpm and yarn as way to bolster software supply chain security by reducing the chance that newly published unreviewed version is immediately pulled into build cooldown periods help add friction and slow down attacks in which bad actor publishes poisoned version of popular package after seizing control of maintainer account thereby preventing rapid spread through manual or automated installations the tradeoff is that legitimate fixes have to wait too unless developers make an exception socket said malicious code also doesn magically become harmless with age release that escapes detection can simply outlast the cooldown the value is in buying researchers maintainers and registries time to act before the next dependency update carries an attack further found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
cleaned_text: an attacker tried to exploit critical gitlab vulnerability on the alpine linux project own gitlab server week after gitlab released fix alpine linux said on 28 october the flaw cve 2026 97229 cvss score 10 can let an attacker run code on gitlab server through crafted regular expression in ci configuration alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account password gitlab fix is set of patches to the ruby that gitlab ships in its own packages and container images alpine gitlab image used standard ruby so upgrading the server to gitlab 19 on 22 october did not fix the flaw for anyone running gitlab on their own ruby built from source or in their own container image upgrading gitlab is not enough alpine said those servers also need ruby 13 12 or later and users of alpine alpinelinux gitlab image need to pull 19 again the server gitlab alpinelinux org hosts aports the repository from which alpine packages are built packages built from 20 to 24 october and the 21 october releases came from aports changes verified against records outside gitlab according to alpine those releases include the minirootfs files that the official alpine docker images are built from alpine is extending the checks to 27 october when it closed the server the keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the gitlab server how the attack unfolded on 13 october alpine upgraded the server to gitlab 19 instead of 19 which it calls mistake the server was still on that version without the 12 october fix when newly registered account began probing it on 20 october the account sent crafted ci configurations to the server on 20 and 21 october they crashed gitlab worker processes times and the main attack on 21 october also caused 502 errors and caused ci jobs to fail in of those crashes the attacker got partway through the exploit and failed at the next step according to alpine the attacker also downloaded alpine gitlab container image which alpine said suggests they were tuning the exploit to our exact build alpine blocked the account on 23 october the attacker came back on 25 and 26 october and tried to get back in but those attempts failed alpine said on 26 october alpine found that the server was still vulnerable after its 22 october upgrade to 19 the next day it closed gitlab to everyone except its developers and build servers and started rebuilding it the rebuild finished on 28 october alpine also replaced gitlab secret keys and the rebuilt server runs ruby 13 or later which has the fix alpine is testing it before reopening it to the public what alpine can and cannot rule out alpine found no sign that the attacker code ran on the server timing probes showed no delays there were no unexpected files keys hooks or processes and no private data was sent back to the attacker via any web or api request that alpine can see it cannot be sure though successful exploit would leave no crash and no trace in the web logs alpine said some logs from the attack day are gone including background job logs and the old container filesystem and neither alpine nor its hosting provider logged outbound network connections because the evidence needed to confirm code execution no longer exists alpine treated the server as compromised and rebuilt it to remove any foothold successful exploit could have left if the attack succeeded these could have been exposed email addresses names and ip addresses of all users password hashes 2fa secrets ci cd variables and runner tokens webhook integration and push mirror credentials personal access tokens which are stored as hashes private repositories and confidential issues and merge requests beyond the password reset and the new secret keys alpine has not said whether runner tokens ci cd variables access tokens or integration credentials stored on the server have been replaced to check its packages alpine confirmed that every aports change added from 20 to 22 october arrived through recorded push by known developer it checked this against records it says the attacker could not reach developer copy of the repository and all 45 build servers every package built from 20 to 24 october came from aports changes as published on git alpinelinux org why the gitlab upgrade did not fix it gitlab compiles the regular expressions in ci configurations with ruby and the bug behind cve 2026 97229 is in onigmo the regular expression engine built into ruby gitlab 12 october release fixed it by patching the ruby inside gitlab linux package and container images ruby own fixed versions came out on 22 and 23 october gitlab upgrade does not change server own ruby so gitlab install on standard ruby keeps the flaw until ruby itself is updated to fixed version as alpine found gitlab fixed linux packages and its official container images carry the patched ruby self compiled install or container image that installs ruby separately as alpine did does not get it as of 29 october neither of gitlab patch release posts for 12 and 21 october tells administrators of self compiled installs to update ruby gitlab self compiled installation guide still lists ruby as its minimum version and ruby reached end of life in april and will get no fix which gitlab servers are exposed gitlab advisory says that under certain conditions the flaw could have allowed an unauthenticated user to run code on the server gitlab com and gitlab dedicated are already patched rapid7 built working exploit in lab and published proof of concept code on 13 october the exploit ran commands as gitlab git user on an unpatched official gitlab 19 image but the same input did not run on the patched 19 image that exploit needs write access first the attacker must commit malicious gitlab ci yml file and file path with utf characters to branch of public project that requirement does not apply on servers where new users can register themselves and create projects in rapid7 tested route only the final ci lint request is unauthenticated gitlab own detection notes also say the attacker must first create that file path through ordinary repository apis rapid7 does not yet know how the attack in the original report to gitlab which is still private avoids the write step alpine has not said how its attacker ci configurations reached gitlab or whether new accounts could create public projects on its server cve 2026 97229 was not in cisa known exploited vulnerabilities catalog as of the catalog 28 october update what gitlab administrators should do gitlab 21 october releases are the newest on each branch listed below and they also fix cve 2026 110264 separate regex flaw branch fixes cve 2026 97229 per gitlab advisory newest release 21 october 19 not listed as affected 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 19 and 18 11 not listed as affected 19 19 10 and 18 11 13 which release fixes server depends on how gitlab is installed gitlab linux package or official container images upgrade to the newest release for your branch self compiled installs or images that install their own ruby upgrade gitlab and update ruby to 13 12 or later ruby will not receive the fix so servers running need to upgrade to one of those versions gitlab advisory named 19 as the fixed version for the 19 branch when it was published on 12 october it now names 19 and lists 19 as affected so servers still on 19 should move to 19 if server cannot be upgraded right away rapid7 suggests restricting anonymous access to public projects stopping untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects or blocking the ci lint route those steps cover only rapid7 exploit route and do not fix the vulnerable regular expression compiler the company said gitlab has published six detection rules for exploitation attempts against self managed servers written in the sigma format four of them which gitlab marks as experimental look for hostile patterns in ci regexp warnings and graphql cilint requests unusually long file paths with non ascii characters and ruby crash reports that point to onigmo the guidance with those rules warns that successful exploit can leave no crash and it gives these further steps look for files owned by the git user in tmp unexpected child processes of puma or sidekiq outbound connections and changed crontabs or ssh keys for the git user if there are signs of code execution treat the server as compromised and rotate the secrets in gitlab secrets json all ci cd variables all runner tokens and all access tokens limit who can create accounts and personal access tokens on the server what alpine users should do account holders will need to set new password with forgot your password on the sign in page when gitlab alpinelinux org reopens alpine said it has also seen automated login attempts against its gitlab using passwords leaked from other sites and anyone who used their gitlab alpinelinux org password elsewhere should change it there users of the alpinelinux gitlab image should pull alpinelinux gitlab 19 again the image published on 27 october contains ruby 13 while any 19 image pulled before then and every older tag is vulnerable alpine own ruby packages already have the fix ruby 12 on alpine 22 23 24 and edge and ruby 13 on alpine 21 running apk upgrade installs it ruby maintainers say the bug matters only for programs that compile regular expression from text an attacker controls and that ruby regexp timeout setting does not protect against it found this article these control systems on controller the attacker can log in as high privileged internal account that is not root when cisco disclosed the flaw in february talos tracked its exploitation as uat 8616 cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023 in cisco traditional key exchange each sd wan router periodically generates an aes key for its traffic and sends it to the catalyst sd wan controller formerly vsmart the controller passes the keys on to other routers process on the controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys on compromised controller keydrift component called littlefilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted for preset list of edge routers it pulls out their ip addresses and 32 byte field talos assesses that field as the aes 256 key material that the controller passes between routers littlefilch encrypts what it collects with rsa and writes it to file it can then send that data over udp to an address listed in settings file which it deletes after reading talos could not recover that settings file the group behind keydrift which talos tracks as uat 11473 has targeted space and satellite services defense and aerospace technology and policy research the group infrastructure overlaps considerably with silent train talos assesses with high confidence silent train is the name lumen black lotus labs uses for network of hacked small office home office iot and business devices lumen says volt typhoon used the network to hide its activity cisa the nsa and the fbi said in 2024 that volt typhoon is chinese state sponsored cyber group talos links uat 11473 to volt typhoon only through the infrastructure overlap it does not say the two are the same group or how uat 11473 relates to uat 8616 the cluster it reported in february separately lumen said on october 28 that volt typhoon was exploiting cve 2026 20127 by late 2025 and continued to exploit it after cisco disclosed the flaw in february lumen does not tie that activity to keydrift keydrift primarily starts via modified runit scripts that cisco sd wan devices use to launch their services according to talos in one version the script for the ssh service starts loader script conf sshd before the real ssh server the conf sshd script writes vdaemon process ids to file and tool called rsshd injects keydrift main module polyflame into each of those processes polyflame runs in memory inside vdaemon it can act as tinyshell like backdoor that runs commands and reads and writes files or as relay that forwards commands between its command server and other machines it is built to accept commands within sd wan control traffic and the analyzed samples contained no hardcoded server address on compromised validator formerly vbond fake aaamgr service under etc sv aaamgr runs packed loader aaamgrd that decrypts and runs polyflame cisco real aaamgr component is python package and does not normally run as compiled service there are also signs of timestomping commands the group ran copied the timestamps and permissions of existing files onto its own files affected releases and fixes cve 2026 20127 affects the catalyst sd wan controller formerly vsmart manager formerly vmanage and validator formerly vbond regardless of their configuration on premises systems are affected as are cisco hosted sd wan cloud deployments including the cisco managed and fedramp environments cisco added the validator to its advisory on june 16 cisco says it is aware of limited exploitation of the flaw to ports 22 and 830 to the ip addresses of known controllers and other known systems cisco says this step worked in test environment but that customers should check how well it works in their own networks such guardrails are already in place for cisco hosted sd wan cloud deployments blocking the ports does not remove malware already on device checking for keydrift talos advises organizations to install cisco fixes follow cisco catalyst sd wan hardening guide and watch for signs of post compromise activity anyone who finds such signs should start incident response and can ask cisco technical assistance center tac for help that advice does not say whether upgrading removes keydrift from device that was already compromised or whether any keys should be replaced cisco february remediation guide for this flaw warns that there could be existing exploits which are still in place from before an upgrade keydrift uses these files and locations some given only by name file the run directory the recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration although dream did not disclose the name of the affected firewall vendor the timing of the advisory combined cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency cisa to add cve 2026 46300 to its known exploited vulnerabilities kev catalog requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by october 31 2026 this
