cleaned_text: attackers can log in to accounts that have no password such as ssh key only accounts on some alpine linux servers running the standard openssh server package they need network access to the server an account name and password between 257 and 024 bytes long openssh which rates the flaw critical released version 10 6p2 today to block it alpine has published fixed packages for every release back to 16 the attack works when the openssh server sshd checks passwords without the pluggable authentication module pam interface password logins are enabled and at least one other account on the machine has password alpine openssh server package is built without pam and password logins are on by default the flaw comes from how sshd works with musl the library that alpine is built on non linux systems linux systems built on glibc and systems that check passwords through pam are not affected said damien miller of the openssh project he told anyone running an affected system to set passwordauthentication no or disable ssh for these systems immediately no attacks using the flaw have been reported who is exposed alpine security advisory lists four conditions server is exposed when all four are true it runs the openssh server package which is built without pam or runs openssh server pam with usepam no passwordauthentication is yes which is the openssh default an account has as its password field which means no password is set at least one other local account has password hash starting with or the attacker also needs the name of an account with no password one account with password is enough to expose every account without one the attack succeeds on every try with single connection according to the advisory on alpine accounts with no password set include key only users created with adduser without password or with usermod users who come from directory service through musl nscd since they have no shadow entry root which has shipped as root in the base image since about alpine 16 the alpine user in the official cloud images built with tiny cloud root is protected by the default permitrootlogin prohibit password setting and can be reached directly only if permitrootlogin yes is set that protection does not help if an exposed account can become root for example through doas the tiny cloud images from 18 11 through 24 give the alpine user passwordless doas they are safe at first boot but become open to attack once any hash exists on the machine for example after an admin sets console password an attacker can then log in as alpine and use doas to become root containers that do not run sshd systems with passwordauthentication no and cloud images set up through cloud init which writes that setting are not affected accounts locked with in etc shadow are not affected either and neither are machines where no account has style password hash the flaw is not limited to alpine zg ltekin of wakefield who reported it names openwrt buildroot and yocto in his technical write up as other musl based systems to check openwrt handles ssh with dropbear by default as its dropbear documentation shows and ltekin says dropbear is not affected on openwrt the flaw can matter only where an admin has installed the openssh server how to fix it on alpine the fix is package update followed by restart because upgrading the package does not restart the running sshd update the packages apk upgrade restart the server rc service sshd restart point releases 21 10 22 23 and 24 already include the fixed package branches 16 to 21 are past their end of support but also got fixed packages cloud instances started from tiny cloud images older than those point releases still need the update or the setting below if you build openssh yourself version 10 6p2 includes the change as its release notes describe if you cannot update yet turning off password logins also stops the attack first make sure your ssh key login works and keep your current session open until new login succeeds then set passwordauthentication no check the configuration with sshd and restart sshd the advisory gives commands that add the setting in drop in file in etc ssh sshd config which alpine default configuration reads from 19 onward they also change every passwordauthentication line in etc ssh sshd config from yes to no including lines inside match block afterward sshd grep passwordauthentication should print passwordauthentication no the advisory suggests looking in var log messages for sshd lines reading accepted password for an account that has no password such as alpine root or key only user on exposed machines also review doas use recently created users files and authorized keys if you cannot rule out login treat the machine as compromised it says why long passwords work without pam sshd checks password itself it hashes the attempt with crypt the library function that turns password into its stored form and compares the result with the stored field an account with no password has only in that field that is too short to hold salt the random prefix of hash so sshd borrows the salt of another account that has real hash for the and hash types musl crypt refuses passwords longer than 256 bytes and returns to signal the error that matches the stored so sshd accepts the login the upper end of the range is sshd own limit of 024 bytes per password this behavior comes from musl change on august 2012 which made failed crypt call return an unmatchable hash rather than null because many programs did not check for failure the 256 byte limit followed on august 29 2012 to protect servers from denial of service attacks the salt borrowing comes from july 15 2016 openssh change that addressed cve 2016 6210 flaw that let attackers learn which usernames exist ltekin says the problem has existed since then the 10 6p2 code change makes sshd refuse match when the stored field is shorter than four characters openssh calls it workaround and says the root and malware delivery including zero click data exfiltration in the chatgpt desktop application eli smadja head of research at check point said in report shared with the hacker news the problem stems from html page previews inside chatgpt code blocks which allow html content to be rendered directly within the application given that executing user supplied html and javascript can introduce security risks of its own the content is placed inside sandbox so that it cannot access data from the app such as cookies and local storage the sandbox also prevents the rendered content from communicating information to an attacker controlled infrastructure however check point found loophole in the manner popup windows are handled during html previews that made it possible to escape the confines of the sandbox and bypass lockdown mode the html preview used nested sandboxed frames and while chatgpt intercepted direct attempts to open new windows the underlying sandbox permissions still allowed popups and permitted them to escape the sandbox smadja explained by creating another nested frame within the rendered page it was possible to access an unmodified popup function and bypass the restrictions placed on the original html preview content opened through this route was no longer subject to the same sandbox restrictions providing way to circumvent the protections of lockdown mode once the restrictions are bypassed threat actor can exploit the vulnerability to exfiltrate data chat messages or deliver malicious payloads by means of crafted prompt malicious gpt or shared chat what more as the attacker is in complete control of the content displayed in the popup window it could be used to render convincing social engineering lures such as fake chatgpt update and trick the victim into downloading malware by persuading them to click on link that said the underlying issue is not limited to the electron based desktop environment highlighting how weakness outside of the scope of the ai model can undermine ai security controls following responsible disclosure the vulnerability was addressed by openai on september 18 2026 lockdown mode was specifically intended to reduce the possibility of data leaving conversation through potentially malicious outbound requests yet weakness in another application feature provided an alternative path around that security boundary smadja said the finding raises broader enterprise security issue ai security controls are only as strong as the wider application environment around them the disclosure comes week after parameter labs out chatgpt com and perform api requests on behalf of the victim this demonstrates how every new feature is chance for more vulnerabilities the company said in statement earlier this september check point also demonstrated covert cross account command channel through which an attacker could use victim chatgpt session to run hidden tasks with the tools data and connected apps available to that session alongside the visible conversation the victim could receive normal answer to their visible request while the attacker task was processed separately and its result returned across accounts check point said the channel operated through code execution environments belonging to different chatgpt accounts the hidden instruction could be delivered through malicious prompt shared chatgpt conversation or custom gpt once it was present in the victim conversation context an ordinary message could trigger the attacker controlled task without revealing it in the visible response the files and send them to an external server from single web page via an indirect prompt injection which hides malicious instructions inside aes encrypted text zero click vulnerability called salesbleed cleaned_text: some wordpress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw according to umut bayram the picus security researcher who found it the update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site old unpatched code so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server the researcher advises blocking web access to the folder random name but the update that installs the fix unpacks its files using the old code already on the site as wordpress updater code shows on sites running or later that old code names the folder after the downloaded file so the name can be predicted one last time before the fix an attacker could use the installer to write new configuration file wp config php into the temporary copy the update would then overwrite the site real file with that file the part of the fix that stops this already works during the update that installs it because wordpress copies the files into place using the new code an attacker who catches the window during that update can still set up the temporary copy of wordpress with their own database log in to it and run php code with the web server permissions before the copy is deleted bayram says in his technical write up from there the attacker can read or write files in the live wordpress site who is exposed during the update not every update exposes the installer the researcher says complete packages always include the installer files smaller partial package built for one specific starting version exposes site only if it happens to packages on through the old code adds random characters to the folder name that hides the name unless the site leaks it some other way such as in an error message the researcher says once or branch fix is installed later updates use random folder name and wp config php file in the temporary copy is never copied over the real one what to do before updating the researcher first recommendation is to stop the web server from serving wp content upgrade at all wordpress works with that folder directly on disk so blocking web access does not break updates he says block the folder in the web server configuration on nginx add location wp content upgrade deny all on apache add require all denied inside directory block for that folder in the virtual host configuration if you can only edit htaccess add redirectmatch 403 wp content upgrade to the htaccess file in the wordpress root above the wordpress rewrite rules do not put an htaccess file inside wp content upgrade itself the old updater deletes everything in that folder before it unpacks an update so the file would be gone when it is needed confirm that request to wp content upgrade returns 403 error update to or to the fixed release for your branch the other safe route he says is manual update done outside the web root the folder the web server serves back up the site files and database unpack the new release in folder the web server does not serve copy the core files into place without touching wp config php or wp content and then run the wordpress database update this way no temporary installer is ever created in folder the web can reach wp cli wp core update command is no substitute because it runs the same updater and unpacks the package into the same folder wordpress and earlier no longer receive security updates so there is no fix for them the researcher says the flaw goes back to wordpress released in 2008 and that those sites should move to supported version attacks and what to check cisa catalog addition wordfence suggests looking for unexpected requests to php files under wp content upgrade administrator accounts no one recognizes plugins no one installed php files in wp content upgrade that no one title: Experts Demonstrate Barracuda Email Security Gateway Chain Enabling Root Access Without Login
cleaned_text: two flaws in barracuda email security gateway an email filtering appliance can be chained to run commands on it as root its highest level of access with no login required the company released patches on monday and the security firm watchtowr detailed the attack chain on thursday one flaw cve 2026 116606 is an authorization bypass an unauthenticated attacker can use it to restore crafted configuration backup and change the appliance global settings the other cve 2026 111560 is command injection it runs commands as root but normally needs an administrator account and on the email security gateway the bypass gives an attacker that access chained the two let an attacker reach root with no login affected products and fixes the authorization bypass affects only the email security gateway the command injection reaches five other products but on those it still needs an administrator account mandiant which assigned the two cve records rates the bypass out of 10 and the command injection barracuda has released patch for each affected product and lists the fixed firmware in its security advisory the email security gateway is fixed in version 030 and later what to do the advisory sets out three steps apply the patch for each affected product or upgrade to the fixed firmware listed above if you cannot patch at once limit the appliance administration interface to trusted internal networks if you have turned automatic patching off switch it back on how the chain works in its technical analysis watchtowr traced the chain through the appliance code failed password change returns the attacker low privilege role instead of stopping the request which leaves backup restore function open to someone who has not logged in that function accepts an uploaded backup and the restored data includes timezone value that the appliance later runs as shell command with root privileges barracuda guards backups with checksum but the secret used to compute it is title: Bitter Hackers Deploy New PapRAT Backdoor in Cyberespionage Campaign Targeting South Asia
cleaned_text: the south asian cyber espionage group known as bitter aka apt 08 apt 37 hazy tiger orange yali apt 17 and ta397 has been observed targeting south asian organizations with previously unreported remote access trojan called paprat paprat has both and rust implementations fortinet fortiguard labs researcher cara lin said its capabilities include command execution file uploads and downloads file deletion directory and drive enumeration and screenshot capture the rust variant adds powershell execution and other commands the campaign is notable for making use of three different infection chains windows shortcut lnk file that abuses the native ftp exe utility to run scripts and create scheduled tasks designed to maintain contact with command and control c2 server vhdx disk image containing lnk file that launches lure microsoft excel spreadsheet while running an msi installer in the background to deploy paprat url shortcut url file that fetches lnk file via webdav which then leads to an msi installer that deploys paprat the living off the land lotl approach is designed to execute commands from remote server goodnfortunes com allowing it to collect directory and task lists directory information from desktop documents and downloads installed antivirus product data and mounted drives the harvested reconnaissance information is saved as abc pdf and exfiltrated back to the c2 server via curl command after which the staged file is deleted from the host second version of the script has been found to retrieve file called talk log from techtalkhelp com the payload contains base64 encoded script to obtain additional instructions from the same server and execute them as powershell commands this staging model gives the attacker operational flexibility while the commands are updated server side without pushing new binary avoiding pe drops and process injection that some security appliances could easily detect fortinet said the paprat malware delivered via the msi installer in the second attack chain is designed for remote control it supports eight commands msg for remote shell fdd for directory listing del for file deletion run for arbitrary file execution gdr for drive enumeration ss1 for screenshot capture upp for uploading local files to the c2 server rivingtonclarks com dww for downloading files from the c2 server rust version of the malware incorporates three more commands ms2 for powershell command execution slp for sleeping and polling resumption bye for process termination notable aspect of the third attack chain is that it combines the salient aspects of the first two sequences by using script to download an msi installer via curl like before the msi installer serves as conduit for paprat which then proceeds to drop wmrat malware previously identified as used by bitter the findings indicate that the threat actor continues to refine its custom arsenal to establish and maintain access to targeted systems these changes underscore the importance of monitoring malicious behavior across scripting tools scheduled tasks and installer activity alongside detecting known malware signatures fortinet said organizations should treat unexpected lnk files url shortcuts disk images and msi packages with caution particularly when delivered through unsolicited messages found this article interesting follow us on google news title: Default 'admin:admin' Server Password Helps Researchers Hack Two Automakers, Unlock and Start Cars
cleaned_text: the login systems behind two car brands mobile apps could be taken over completely two security researchers found allowing them to access any customer account and for an owner with connected car unlock the doors and start the engine both apps signed customers in through forgerock an identity platform now part of ping identity and on those servers the researchers reached an administrator console that still used its default password they tested the full attack only on their own and consenting owners cars in the united states in february 2026 and both systems were fixed about two hours after they reported the problem shubham shah and sam curry published their work late last week they had started with the apps both brands signed customers in through the same platform which runs in two parts one for login and one called openidm that holds customer records openidm comes with built in administrator console powered by the apache felix tool forgerock own hardening guide tells operators to remove this console or protect it before going live because it stores its own password separately from the rest of the system on these servers it was still there and still used the documented default the word admin for both the username and the password the console was blocked from the open internet but the edge that guards the site and the java software behind it read the same web address differently by adding encoded slashes and extra characters the researchers made the edge treat the request as harmless static file while the server treated it as the path to the console and the default password did the rest the full method is in their technical analysis inside the console the researchers used built in scheduler to run small scripts that execute their own code on the identity server that gave them command prompt on the machine that holds the customer records for both brands logins the records sat behind the same block as the console but the researchers code reached them from inside the server they changed target account email address and password signed in as that customer through the normal app and received the same access tokens the real app uses those tokens were the keys to the car using the account own vehicle commands the researchers unlocked the doors and started the engine of test car with the owner standing next to it then stopped the engine and locked it again the researchers were careful about what they had shown they reported being able to open session for any customer account on the affected servers but they ran the vehicle commands only on cars they owned or were allowed to use they said they tested the complete chain only with us accounts and vehicles shubham shah published second attack on the australian systems behind the same brands there the way in was different admin credentials for the identity server had been left in the app code intended for test setup he set out the full australia chain in separate post with both attacks together the researchers said they could send unlock and engine start commands to the brands cars in australia the united states and canada that second post does not give date for when the australian systems were fixed the attack left little for an owner to notice changing the email and password did not log the owner out of their app and the researchers could direct the account alerts to their own phone keeping them off the owner phone the researchers put the real email address back after the test neither write up says whether anyone else found or used the path before it was closed what identity teams should check the brands mistake was in how they ran forgerock not new bug in the product so there is no cve the public id that tracks flaw and no vendor advisory to follow the console and its default password have been documented for years and the maker production hardening guide already tells operators to remove the console or change its password before going live for teams running the same identity software now sold as pingidm two checks matter look for the apache felix console at system console and remove it or change its default password do not count on edge or waf path rules to hide an admin page path the edge and the server read differently can slip past the rules as it did here the two researchers have long record of this kind of work usually breaking into the web systems behind the apps rather than the cars themselves they have shown remote access to vehicles from honda kia and subaru among others subaru flaw they reported exposed owners accounts and their cars through that carmaker connected car service and broader 16 brand study in 2023 found the same kind of web weakness across much of the industry found this article interesting follow us phrase backup list of 12 or 24 words or hardware wallet are not affected the wallet maker said it has paused google and apple sign in while it investigates what affected users should do the wallet maker has given this user guidance for accounts created with google or apple login do not send new funds to the account do not re import the account or recreate it anywhere move any funds that are not staked or locked to an account that uses recovery phrase or hardware wallet trust updates only from the official accounts of the wallet maker and the login provider and ignore direct messages or links that offer recovery staked and locked assets are taking longer to secure the wallet maker is also working with the login provider on way for users to check whether their account was affected in the meantime the login provider has published recovery address list which it says lets people tell its own transfers apart from possibly malicious ones it has also warned users not to assume that an unfamiliar destination address is linked to the attacker what went wrong in an incident update web3auth said security issue in its own infrastructure affected certain wallets it provides inside the keplr app keplr went further saying the flaw led to private key breach for some users who signed in with google or apple private key is the secret code that approves payments from wallet so whoever holds it can move the money neither company has said how the flaw worked when the attacker first used it or whether that route is now closed where the money went no dollar figure for the theft has provider calls secure recovery wallets on 11 blockchains in the cosmos family and eight ethereum style chains bitquery blockchain data firm counted at least 01 million moving from more than 44 000 wallets into the recovery wallets by late last week the firm first reported the transfers as theft it has since issued corrected analysis that treats them as the rescue though it says it cannot check maker warned users the moved funds are safe the login provider said in its recovery thread and it is working with the wallet maker to return them to users it has not said how or when beyond keplr the title: Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records
cleaned_text: single attacker using ai agents pulled emergency dispatch records covering seven taipei districts researchers at acronis threat research unit said last week the agents also found taipei certificate repair utilities oceangate 2025 2026 which primarily focuses on asian organizations with variant of sparrowdoor after obtaining initial access via internet facing linux servers and then indonesia according to report published by positive technologies in august 2026 there are indications that the campaign has also targeted entities in egypt and the philippines using this method the javascript injected into the compromised websites is heavily obfuscated using jsjiami publicly available javascript obfuscation service check point said it first checks whether the user is running title: Beyond the Alert: The Case for Rich Network Data
cleaned_text: at some point your security will fail this isn pessimism it not because your team and tools aren sophisticated enough it the reason we have detections in the first place and it why once we accept that prevention has its limits we arrive at an interdiction strategy finding and disrupting what got in after the alert the alert tells you something happened however gaining access to your network doesn necessarily mean attackers have stolen data or disrupted the systems they were targeting they may need to obtain additional access move to another machine or further explore the network being able to see and understand that activity is the intervention opportunity people naturally gravitate toward detections during product evaluations they re tangible easy to compare and quantify and address the question everyone wants an answer to will they catch the attack there often an assumption that the rest will follow meaning if the detections are good surely the investigation will be as well right whether you can trace the attack understand the scope and respond in time to intervene depends largely on the data behind that detection in network security product can have good detections and still leave an analyst struggling to investigate perhaps the analyst can see the connection that triggered the alert but can follow what happened next if search returns nothing does that mean the activity didn happen or that you weren collecting the evidence needed to see it this and the arrival of ai defense is why data quality has recently been getting so much attention data vs data investigation success takes knowledge of both attacker behavior and your own environment you need to understand what you re looking for but also what your data can actually tell you the difference in network data shows up when investigating an alert both shallow and rich data provide investigations with starting point but one can rapidly lead to dead end shallow data is often just composed of timestamps ips and basic connection information rich data retains greater transaction details and adds context it correlates and lets you pivot and reconstruct answering not just what triggered the alert but what happened before after and elsewhere to evaluate the data quality of security tool consider key questions such as are full transaction details provided or just summary is packet content or file extraction available how far back can we search and how fast can follow connection across hosts and time ai data ai powered soc tools can now process data at scale that human teams simply cannot match the more data points ai has the more effectively it can surface events while shallow data limits what ai can correlate richer data allows it to identify subtle patterns across hosts and behaviors potentially exposing previously unseen indicators of compromise or providing opportunity to intervene before an attack escalates ai can help when something unfamiliar is encountered nobody knows every service process or log format an assistant can help explain what you re looking at suggest questions to pursue or write script to make large set of data easier to examine that can save lot of research time it can also help an analyst get past point where they would otherwise be stuck but we re certainly not at the point where we can trust what ai claims 100 of the time you still need to test what it gives you if an assistant suggests an explanation check whether the evidence supports it if it produces query or script test what it does and before running suggested command ask what else it might affect model can be so focused on solving the immediate problem that it overlooks the rest of the system as ai takes on more investigative work the ability to inspect the underlying evidence becomes another essential aspect of modern data quality unfamiliar territory is the test when evaluating data from network security products ndr in particular take an alert from demonstration and investigate it properly but don follow the guided path dig deep and put yourself in unfamiliar territory you ll get much better sense of how the product helps analysts when they re dealing with an event they haven seen before look at the transactions behind the alert ask what packet content or extracted files are available follow the activity backwards and forwards in time ask question that wasn anticipated these questions and tasks probably won be part of typical demo that the point they ll let you see if the data provides the fidelity reach and context to actually solve investigations or just starting point with nowhere to go detections get the attention but data determines the outcome the real question is can your team use the data to fully understand an incident and decide what title: Russian Turla Hackers Use New Cereal Malware to Steal Emails From Government Exchange Servers
cleaned_text: the russia aligned state sponsored threat actor known as turla aka snake is wielding previously undocumented cyber espionage toolset called cereal that used to break into victims microsoft exchange servers with an aim to surreptitiously collect emails according to an eset report shared with the hacker news ahead of publication the sophisticated and modular tool is designed for long term intelligence gathering and has been observed against two governmental entities in kazakhstan and romania in late 2025 the cereal toolset is carefully constructed instrument for long term stealthy cyber espionage the slovakian cybersecurity company said it leaves little on disk avoids external infrastructure that could be discovered and blocked and conceals itself within legitimate exchange processes the cereal toolset demonstrates that for turla exchange servers are not just mail servers they are durable collection points internal execution hubs and suitable environment for hiding sophisticated net tradecraft the toolset is collection of interconnected components that are capable of running on microsoft exchange servers receiving commands executing them in memory mapping the infected network and harvesting emails of interest the initial access vector used to deliver the malware is unknown although the group is known to conduct spear phishing watering hole and isp level adversary in the middle aitm attacks cereal gets its name from the fact that the tools make extensive use of serialization which refers to the process of converting data structure or an object state into format that can be easily stored transmitted and reconstructed number of aspects make the malware stand apart absence of an external command and control c2 infrastructure instead abusing compromised exchange server for this purpose sending commands in the form of separate compiled net programs using an automated email collection module which is injected into legitimate microsoft exchange processes and is engineered to manipulate the email transport pipeline the combination of these techniques shows that the threat actor possesses deep understanding of the internal workings of microsoft exchange eset added the cereal framework consists of eight moving parts that work together to provide the attackers with access to sensitive email data cerealrunner which is deployed by the operator and serves as pathway for dropping additional components including cerealloader cerealsprinter cerealiron and cerealmoth cerealloader which loads and runs net assembly from an encrypted file on disk leading to the execution of cerealsprinter cerealsprinter which functions similarly to cerealrunner and is used to decrypt and run cerealneuron cerealhermit and cerealbox cerealiron an injector that makes it possible to load and run net assemblies from non net processes cerealmoth which receives an assembly and method name as inputs loads the assembly and runs the specified method cerealneuron passive backdoor that runs on compromised exchange server and listens for incoming web requests on paths that appear like regular exchange traffic to execute assemblies contained in cerealrunner binaries cerealhermit variant of cerealneuron that reads commands from encrypted files on disk and has no network functionality of its own cerealbox which is the email harvesting module that processes filters and collects email messages by injecting itself into the exchange transport service edgetransport exe upon gaining visibility into the email flow the malware looks for messages containing doc docx or pdf attachments and matches at least one of many hard coded lists with sender addresses recipient addresses subject lines or attachment names emails that meet the filtering criteria are compressed encrypted and staged in files on disk after which they are exfiltrated and deleted via cerealneuron commands in the attack aimed at the romanian government organization cerealbox is said to have been configured to gather emails involving nato and european union institutional addresses pattern that aligns with russia strategic priorities the commands delivered as compiled net programs are handled by cerealrunner which unpacks and executes the payloads in memory and then sends the results back to cerealneuron for subsequent exfiltration to the threat actor in encrypted format the commands support retrieving mailboxes or specific messages queuing active directory for computers users groups and dns records running windows management instrumentation wmi queries extracting lsa secrets listing volume snapshots and performing file operations the sheer volume of near identical binaries each compiled for specific task strongly suggests that the operators have an internal framework that automates the compilation and packaging of commands eset researcher mat as porolli said combined with codebase built around modular interchangeable components the title: France Blames Iran for Sabotage Attack on Refrigeration Controllers at About 700 Retail Sites
cleaned_text: an october cyberattack on refrigeration controllers at about 700 french retail sites was carried out by cyber unit of iran islamic revolutionary guard corps irgc the french government said yesterday the attackers broke into controllers on the night of october 11 and changed their defrost settings to high temperatures that caused food losses and in at least 15 cases fires the unit is called shahid kaveh it is known mainly through hacktivist personas such as cyberaveng3rs and cyber isnaad front that publicly claim some of its attacks france says france foreign ministry plans to summon iran ambassador and to ask its european partners to adopt new sanctions against iranian organizations and individuals involved in the attack the paris prosecutor office opened judicial investigation yesterday against the unit head the head two deputies and anyone else identified it has asked for international arrest warrants the offenses under investigation include illegally interfering with computer systems and causing damage by means dangerous to people both made more serious by the aim of serving foreign power iran in the october attack the attackers took remote control of danfoss and dixell refrigeration controllers through web interfaces the prosecutor office said in press release they started abnormal defrost cycles with no time limit and switched off the temperature probes safety alerts which should go off above certain temperature the attack caused about 20 fires most of the organizations hit were large retailers according to joint report by france cyber crisis coordination center known as c4 they include casino leclerc coop rative metro carrefour and intermarch small butcher shops slaughterhouse and cooperative food plants were also among the victims the center also tied the attack to the simultaneous targeting of schneider electric equipment at several small hydroelectric installations in france the effects on that equipment were moderate in its attribution statement the ministry estimated the food losses at several tens of millions of euros and called the operation the first offensive cyber campaign on french soil carried out purely for sabotage how france tied the attack to iran the c4 brings together france national cybersecurity agency anssi the dgse and dgsi security services the armament directorate and the cyber defense command it says four indicators point to the irgc as the sponsor of the attack and to shahid kaveh as the unit that carried it out the infrastructure used in the attack was also used during the same period for reconnaissance of schneider electric equipment that equipment is installed at sites such as small and medium sized energy and water production sites the reconnaissance relied on techniques that shahid kaveh has used since at least april the attackers also used fofa scanning tool they usually use cyberbannews propaganda outlet linked to the unit reported on the attack as early as october 13 the attack infrastructure also held traces of persian prosecutors said the criminal investigation run by france anti cybercrime office ofac and the dgsi found an attack method typical of the unit it also found the use of persian and ip addresses leading to devices located in iran shahid kaveh has previously claimed attacks on industrial equipment according to c4 through cyberaveng3rs it claimed an earlier campaign against unitronics an israeli company that makes industrial control systems in november 2023 in march and april it claimed large sabotage campaign against israeli and interests that hit industrial control equipment including israeli refrigeration equipment france attribution does not mention the new wave of refrigeration attacks that struck supermarkets in several other european countries last week what operators should do france cert fr said in an incident alert that it was aware of numerous compromises affecting remote refrigeration controllers across four product families they are the danfoss ak sm and ak sc series the copeland xweb and the dixell xweb the alert last updated on october 16 warned that attack campaigns against this equipment were probably still underway and that exposing management interface to the internet goes against good practice for controllers that are not compromised the alert steps are remove internet exposure from these units and from any unit reachable at public ip address check insurance contract terms before cutting off the data feed to the refrigeration contractor review the full configuration especially the defrost ranges restore access only through secure vpn or protected network in an emergency filtering the contractors ip addresses at firewall is possible but it is not lasting fix follow the maker recommended practices for danfoss devices this includes updating firmware setting the security level to strict and ensuring default passwords have been changed for compromised controllers the steps are remove internet exposure and check insurance terms as above restart danfoss equipment or otherwise restore the device to its factory settings restore access only through secure vpn or protected network as above firewall filtering of contractors ip addresses is an emergency option not lasting fix reconfigure the device before putting it back into service then follow the maker recommended practices an end of life eol device that receives no security fixes faces very high risk of compromise if it remains exposed to the internet the alert warns in that case factory reset alone is not enough it removes the attackers persistence but the device stays vulnerable and will almost certainly be compromised again found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
cleaned_text: cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of campaign in which an emerging agentic penetration testing platform called antifox has been used to steal amazon web services aws credentials and pivot laterally into compromised environments in several recently observed intrusions alibaba cloud systems hosting antifox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet facing web services and associated aws environments arctic wolf labs said in report shared with the hacker news the activity has been observed chaining together web exploitation and web shell deployment to facilitate configuration discovery credential validation cloud service enumeration secret access and storage operations antifox available for download from github has been described as an artificial intelligence ai driven autonomous penetration testing platform as of writing the project has been forked 251 times and starred 474 times on its readme page the project maintainer states given an authorized target planner worker main agent multi agent system runs the full engagement over dual graph core global asset graph per task exploration graph recon attack surface discovery exploitation finding capture report delivery fully observable interactive and deliverable unlike most automated pentest tools that are great at discovery but stop at discovery antifox puts its weight on delivery turning what the ai finds into report that an engineer can understand reproduce back with evidence and hand straight to the client according to arctic wolf some of the initial access activity is associated with compromised internet facing internet information services iis application the access is then leveraged to create an aspx web shell using w3wp exe the iis worker process and run operating system commands to perform the following actions run powershell commands to locate web config files and configuration backups read application settings and database connection strings enumerate debug and error log directories attempts to connect to an internal production database using credential extracted from the application configuration copy configuration and log files into web accessible upload directory on compromised iis server commands run through w3wp exe identified the execution context with whoami enumerated the application directory checked permissions with icacls and tested the ability to write files into the web root arctic wolf said the creation of an aspx web shell by w3wp exe followed by command execution through the same iis worker process suggests compromise through the affected web application the precise vulnerability used to achieve code execution on the iis server is not known in other attacks the threat actor is said to have started with valid aws credential obtained through as yet undetermined means antifox demo specifically this involved abusing valid iam identities to validate credentials and enumerate dozens of services including iam ec2 s3 lambda secrets manager kms rds ecs eks redshift athena glue systems manager api gateway cloudwatch cloudformation dynamodb and amazon bedrock while majority of these authenticated cross service api requests ended up with an accessdenied error some of the discovery and secret access operations were successful according to the cybersecurity company in at least some instances the activity has been observed progressing beyond secrets manager enumeration to successful getsecretvalue request against production secret elsewhere valid aws identity was used for s3 discovery and object operations via api calls agentic frameworks such as these make penetration testing techniques more accessible to threat actors while increasing the speed and consistency with which these techniques can be applied in live attacks arctic wolf said the rise of ai tools in cyber attacks the disclosure comes as threat actors are increasingly weaponizing ai powered penetration testing tools like artex to conduct broad scale attacks across the world enabling them to automate various stages of an intrusion with minimal human intervention the integration of ai has allowed adversaries both large and small to adapt established tradecraft and deploy them at machine speed making it possible to progress from scanning github for secrets to exfiltrating data from an azure key vault in five minutes earlier this week vecert disclosed details of campaign dubbed operation ghost campus orchestrated by chinese threat actor that uses ai agents to maintain perpetual cost free access to large language models llms and eventually perform automated academic fraud and steal data belonging to over 000 students enrolled at the fengxian campus the agent industrializes the creation of accounts on the search engine fofa info scans the global cyberspace for misconfigured servers extracts api keys for openai and deepseek automatically verifies their financial balances and injects them into the attacker development environment vecert said this stolen computing power fuels an interactive gotty terminal pi ai coding assistant and by extension provides intelligence to the scripts that sustain academic fraud bots heartbeat bots and extractors of financial data and personally identifiable information pii belonging to thousands of students at the fengxian campus according to data from censys there are 465 hosts running an exposed artex console as of november 2026 with most of them located in the hong kong china japan singapore and south korea however it worth noting that not every instance is necessarily malicious in nature in separate report check point research said it identified 557 systems that hosted artex including 10 misconfigured instances exposing their full databases in many observed cases artex required remarkably little interaction from its operators once an objective had been established check point said rather than continuously directing attacks step by step operators frequently issued goal and left the agent fleet to work toward it human interactions were largely limited to checking progress asking whether target had been compromised or occasionally adjusting priorities the vast majority of the attacks are designed to siphon cryptocurrency steal apple code signing certificates compromise gaming accounts and conduct denial of service dos attacks against gambling websites the activity has been found to exploit vulnerabilities related to weak or hard coded passwords missing authentication insecure direct object references and remote code execution in the campaign targeting apple code signing certificates artex agents searched compromised systems for certificate databases followed by validating the stolen certificates by checking passwords private keys apple revocation status expiration dates and associated provisioning profiles ultimately the activity is estimated to have harvested more than 300 certificates and their passwords out of which three certificates passed the full validation process and could be used to sign arbitrary ios applications the biggest change brought by agentic hacking to the cyber threat landscape is scale and speed check point cautioned as cybercriminal with limited technical skills can task ai agents with investigating number of targets in parallel and exploiting them using known and zero day vulnerabilities with less manual effort its relevance to us lies in its scale speed and persistence cert eu said in an alert artex can test large numbers of low complexity misconfigurations including those human tester would notice but not have time to check and it can work through long attack chains without the fatigue that limits manual testing the same is true of complex payload crafting exploitation paths that need carefully tailored payloads often take more effort than the severity of the finding justifies so manual assessment may leave them untested tools like antifox and artex are part of broader set of about 45 open source agentic attack frameworks that are engineered to connect to an llm and can act on outputs autonomously they fall under five broad categories network kill chain capable of end to end reconnaissance exploitation and post exploitation pentagi redamon and darkmoon web app and api strix shannon and pentestgpt c2 integrated sage echidna pojun and forang harnesses raptor cyberstrike cyber harness nebula and cybermes research prototypes incalmo hackingbuddygpt vulnbot hacksynth autopt and ares each framework has public source code and wires model into loop that runs tools and acts on their output gitguardian said agentic ai pentesting tools hand their agent shell and web access so the model can assemble pipeline at runtime title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
cleaned_text: we tell customers three things about securing ai agents they need their own identities access that fits the job they re given and traceability that separate from any human that was true for us at token as well then we built an agent that broke all three by default this helped us think through how such agents should be defended when browser agent acts inside user authenticated session the application may see the user but not the agent the delegation or the task intended scope by creating an agent that breaks all the security rules token learned how companies should be using identity to gain control especially as agent use scales standards are coming but there are steps security teams can take today the agent we would have flagged the agent we created is named rehearsal its job is to answer questions inside the token platform by doing rather than telling it autonomously opens pages in the browser tab sets filters and fills in forms from security perspective it typical ui agent that runs in the user browser that what makes it useful but it also means the agent runs within the user session and has their reach moreover to the server behind the page the agent clicks are inherently indistinguishable from the user because nothing in session cookie points to who the session driver is what controlling both sides made possible because token owns both the agent and the app it runs we can close each gap from the inside for example token knows who driving the session because rehearsal tells it who is we learned that there are multiple best practices that you can apply when you control the ai agent itself while the agent moves dim and lock the application and clearly indicate who has control record every move for each session including those that were blocked reduce the agent reach below the user for rehearsal we ensure the dashboards are read only it can save anything without the user approval doesn fill in secret fields and never sends call that the platform has refused it also understands the dashboard controls through the page accessibility labels this works for our own agent but only because it relies on access that no outside agent has who has to fix it for everyone else we could give rehearsal an actor scope and page map because we re the ones who wrote it browser agent driving your crm or your cloud console has none of that the app can tell that it there and the agent can tell which field holds secret or which button deletes record the session itself carries the user identity the way out is to give agents their own lanes separate from human users the web has started building them but it isn necessarily focused on holistic approaches the browser can mark when its agent is driving and restrict itself accordingly chrome auto browse for example already requires person approval before high stakes actions such as payments or mass emails limits its agent to the sites the task requires and tags the pages the agent visits in the user history microsoft lets admins turn agentic browsing on per site and pause it before passwords and card numbers are entered the app can publish its actions as tools webmcp draft that google and microsoft are writing in w3c community group lets site expose actions that an agent can call directly and flag each one as read only or consequential that way the agent doesn need to guess what button does the agent can sign its requests web bot auth now an ietf working group draft lets site verify which agent sent request what missing is layer that connects them each lane knows something the others don and none of them passes it on the browser knows its agent is driving but neither chrome nor edge describes how to tell the app on the other end webmcp tool runs inside the user session with the user rights so it doesn by itself narrow what the agent can reach web bot auth names the agent but the draft makes it plain that it doesn cover delegation so it omits the person the agent works for the app ends up holding on to pieces of context rather than delivering something actionable now consider that the agents are arriving faster than the standards agent friendly isn enough on its own every lane built for agents should carry the agent identity verifiable link to the person it acts for and scope narrower than that person together those three signals give an application the minimum context it needs to make an authorization decision otherwise faster lane is just faster path to the misuse of privilege what security teams can do before standards catch up waiting for standardization is not an option you need to start discovering agentic browsers and extensions as soon as possible including the users whose sessions they borrow and while you can tell who clicked you can choose which clicks need person by adding step up check such as passkey prompt inventory browser agents agentic extensions and endpoint agents that can act through authenticated sessions and map them to users and owners trace every ai agent consumer so you know which people and other agents are using each individual agent review every identity that each individual agent has access to identify potential attack paths that use agents to bypass access controls require explicit approval or step up authentication before sensitive or irreversible application actions ask critical saas vendors whether their audit records distinguish agent activity from human activity and whether they support task scoped delegation until browsers and applications can carry agent identity human delegation and task scope together companies should treat every agent using human session as delegated access that must be discovered constrained and audited found this article interesting this article is title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
cleaned_text: the in house python script behind emudhra october key compromise has now cost the company more of its intermediate certificate authorities cas even though it did not weaken their keys each intermediate ca has its own private key which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues the intermediate cas compromised in october had different problem single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte the company said this week the script also retrieved the rsa keys of the newly revoked cas from the company hardware security modules hsms the company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules it revoked the cas late last week the company had called those cas unaffected the rsa issuers went through different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted it wrote on mozilla bug tracker on october 19 of the were for website tls certificates and for code signing the company had put of them into production in may its list names 195 certificates from them 29 for its own domains both problems began at key ceremony on april 30 2025 according to the full incident report the company posted to the same bug tracker this week that day it generated 16 ca keys on utimaco hsms including the behind the october key compromise the keys were meant for crypto4a hsms at the company us and eu sites moving keys between hsms from different vendors is limited the company says so its pki operations team wrote the python script to wrap each key for transport and unwrap it again the round trip that day was practice run of the transfer and the source hsm fips approved mode was switched off for it as an approved exception after the round trip the script read each private key out of the hsm into the ceremony computer memory and rebuilt the key from that copy for the ecdsa keys single line in that read back truncated the private value to its leading byte the report says the rebuilt key carried label almost identical to the original which allowed the weak copy to be sent for signing and certification the hacker news worked out all keys from their public certificates the smallest for em ov tls ca g3c is and the largest is 237 nothing in the ceremony tested the key strength or checked the certified key against the first generated key the weak keys still produced valid signatures and their certificates passed linting and webtrust audit cycles unnoticed the hsms worked correctly throughout according to the company which puts the fault in its own script and process controls invalid crl signatures in june 2025 were an early sign of the same fault according to the report the company fixed them at the time by re signing the lists with the keys that matched the certificates which were the weak ones according to the report the rsa keys went through the same read back step that the company earlier response had ruled out early last week the company said its earlier answers reflected only what its teams had gathered so far including which script paths each set of keys took the script did not shorten those keys and every signature still checks against the certified key but their private parts such as the private exponent and one of the primes sat in the memory of python process on the ceremony computer as result the company cannot positively demonstrate that this key material was in compliance with cps its own rule on moving keys into and out of an hsm logs and files from that computer cannot reliably show how the material was handled the company reached that view in early november after discussions with browser root programs the rsa cas were revoked late last week with the reason code cessationofoperation not the ca compromise code used when the first were revoked on october 18 participants in the bug thread have asked why the company chose that code rather than keycompromise of the 195 certificates in the company certificate list 130 came from em dv tls ca g2c 63 from em ov tls ca g2c and from the code signing ca em ov cs ca g2c besides the company own domains the certificates name several universities and colleges county and other organizations the newest was issued last week days before the cas were revoked all their holders have been moved to new certificates the company says the company says the wrap and unwrap process was used only this once and that its other key ceremonies all created keys in place participants in the bug thread also want the script published and some have asked how private keys could leave its hsms at all kpmg which the company hired as an independent reviewer is due to finish by december the company inventory of all its ca keys is due november 30 the company knows of no case of misuse anyone holding one of the october keys could have impersonated any website according to disclosure site run by dennis jackson who investigated the keys for mozilla browsers that enforce certificate transparency could not have been fooled whether anyone used the keys against software that skips that check is not known what emsign certificate holders need to check emudhra which sells certificates under the emsign brand is exiting the publicly trusted tls business following its october 22 announcement holders can find affected certificates in the company list or by searching certificate transparency logs for the revoked g2c tls issuers all issuance from the company g1 hierarchy is due to stop before november 16 as the remaining customers mainly university federation in north america move to another provider microsoft will start removing the 10 remaining emudhra roots including emsign root ca g1 on november 16 according to an update to its security response post earlier this week certificates that chain to those roots will then lose default trust in windows and edge and in some of its other products on their own timelines according to the indian company phase out schedule chrome and firefox will not trust g1 certificates issued after november 16 and apple will end trust in all g1 certificates including older ones on november 30 macos 27 26 and 15 stop bundled command line tools such as curl and git from accepting the compromised tls ca certificates apple said in support note earlier this week they also drop roots including emsign root ca g1 from etc ssl cert pem title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
cleaned_text: microsoft on tuesday released patches for total of 259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 000 flaws these cover 726 flaws in windows 174 in office 61 in developer tools 59 in sql server 53 in developer tools and 27 in sharepoint server the patches also include 165 non microsoft issued cve identifiers more than 500 flaws relate to elevation of privilege followed by remote code execution and information disclosure bugs with the latest round of fixes microsoft has addressed over 100 cves this year alone according to satnam narang senior staff research engineer at tenable of these moderate severity security flaw in microsoft outlook cve 2026 124194 cvss score has been flagged as actively exploited by microsoft product ui does not warn users of unsafe actions in microsoft office outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over network microsoft said in an advisory an unauthenticated attacker could send specially crafted message file and persuade target to open it in an affected version of microsoft outlook this in turn could cause outlook to connect to an attacker controlled network location without displaying the usual external content warning potentially disclosing authentication information such as an ntlmv2 hash that could be used to impersonate the user microsoft emphasized that successful exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction the tech giant credited researcher named nono and anthropic beno sevens using claude with discovering and reporting the flaw email is the easiest door into any company and this flaw turns one opened file into stolen identity jack bicer director of vulnerability research at action1 said captured hash can let an attacker sign in as the victim read their data and move to other systems they can reach the moderate label undersells this one attackers are already exploiting it it needs only one click on an email file and it hits outlook which nearly every organization runs stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox that said redmond has not attributed the activity to particular threat actor or provided technical details on how the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild the advisory also doesn spell out whether the discovery came before or after attackers began exploiting the flaw the development has prompted the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency cisa to add the flaw to its known exploited vulnerabilities kev catalog requiring federal agencies to apply the fix by schannel cve 2026 119952 windows virtual filtering platform cve 2026 95962 and windows xbox live networking service cve 2026 112967 as well as privilege escalation flaw in azure openai cve 2026 119990 jake knott head of threat intelligence at watchtowr said teams are really starting to feel the strain of working out what actually matters when there is fire after fire every day demanding immediate attention start with what you actually have exposed to the internet then what already being exploited in the wild and only then everything else before going into panic mode check whether you even use title: Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges
cleaned_text: ai provider keys that customers stored on railway were stolen in an october breach and used to commit an estimated 740 000 in unauthorized spending the platform as service provider said yesterday it has promised to pay those charges itself when an ai provider will not refund them the company builds and runs apps for its customers and stores their secrets such as api keys and database credentials as environment variables the attacker decrypted variables in at most 85 of workspaces about 100 000 and its database queries looked for ai provider keys in an october 26 update the company told customers asking about refunds for unauthorized ai spend that railway is unable to refund customers for spend performed with compromised api keys it encouraged them to contact the ai providers directly and offered to escalate their requests according to the company incident report the decrypted data also included linked account tokens for 852 users byok agent keys and github oauth tokens all were reset each user was notified and no logins to customer accounts using stolen credentials were found in addition to ai keys one of the attacker database queries matched cloud database and payment service credentials the company forensics did not show any customer databases being accessed and there was no indication that customers code repositories were downloaded the attacker also read the stored histories of 353 builds including the variables and secrets passed to those builds the company logs show which environments were exposed but not which variables so the figure of about 100 000 workspaces is an upper limit it emailed customers it judged to be at high risk any data the attacker copied but did not decrypt can no longer be decrypted because the credential the attacker used has been disabled according to the company what railway customers can do refund terms differ by ai provider according to the company incident report aws bedrock aws existing refund policy covers fraud and its account teams have started refunds google gemini google existing refund policy covers fraud and its account teams have started refunds openai refunds are reviewed on case by case basis customers file claim with openai then pass the case id to railway support team spacexsi refunds are reviewed on case by case basis and customers submit their claims to the same support team anthropic talks are still underway and the platform will cover costs from breached anthropic keys in the meantime openrouter it maintains its no refund policy in its terms of service so the platform will cover all openrouter related costs resulting from the breach customers are asked to report charges they did not make through charge report form the form says the company is not responsible for usage of these keys but is investigating the theft and working with the providers the report does not say how the 740 000 figure was estimated or what period it covers neither it nor the form sets cap or deadline for claims or states whether customers must pay disputed charges while claim is under review the company advises customers to revoke and replace any sensitive variable stored on the platform before october 21 keys should be revoked or rotated with the provider that issued them since filing charge report does not revoke key it also advises removing public network access to databases checking github audit logs and which apps can access the account and checking audit logs in registries such as docker hub most of this advice dates from the company october disclosure and report it published the next day out of caution the company also gave some providers every key it held for their services so reset requests reached more than 100 000 users revocation notice from provider does not by itself mean key was exposed how the railway breach happened the attack began in the company build system according to its incident report at 07 28 utc on october 20 the attacker exploited previously unknown flaw to partly escape the filesystem isolation around build and read some files on the host virtual machine that gave the attacker credential that build servers use to push finished images and reach some internal systems the on call engineer was paged at 13 58 utc about six and half hours after the first exploit when an alert flagged unusual calls to registry service the credential was meant only for build work but the company internal temporal system which drives parts of the build process accepted it as trusted client through it the attacker read some stored histories of other builds the same credential could also fetch cached snapshots of code that gave the attacker copy of the company internal monorepo the code base that many of its services deploy from the company says the copy showed the attacker how the platform works and helped them find exploits and move quickly between systems after scanning that code the attacker found wrongly configured oidc binding in one of the company cloud environments the binding is part of how its deployment system obtains short lived cloud credentials and at 03 26 utc on october 21 the attacker exploited the mistake to obtain one with that credential the attacker took two more from the cloud environment one could read encrypted variables from production database when used inside the internal network and the other was an ssh key the ssh key opened machine that runs orchestration tasks for the company fleet that machine stored credential capable of decrypting customer variables which it needed to start customer workloads each environment variables are encrypted with that environment own key and those keys are in turn encrypted by root key stored in cloud provider key management service kms between 04 07 and 05 21 utc on october 21 the attacker pulled encrypted variables from the database looking for names that matched ai provider keys using the orchestration machine credentials with the kms it decrypted some of them between 04 42 and 05 14 utc and again between 06 36 and 07 15 utc the attacker was fully removed from the company systems at 09 24 utc that day those times differ from the company preliminary report of october 22 which dated the attack from 13 58 utc on october 20 and placed decryption after 05 27 utc each build now runs in its own short lived virtual machine on top of the old isolation its credentials can push only one specific image to the company registry within an hour of the company patching the original escape its own hardening team built second exploit by changing that attack that was one reason the company moved every user to the new build system at once every weakness the attacker used is now closed the company says it has filed complaint with the fbi ic3 and is working with specialist forensics firm whose investigation continues it is sharing indicators of compromise privately for now and plans to publish them once law enforcement agrees the company believes the stolen credentials were used by services that relay or resell access to ai providers for use in distillation it has not established whether the attacker ran those services nor has it named the attacker in their black october analysis wiz researchers list this breach among incidents disclosed in october by at least nine ai developer platforms including the earlier opencode breach every public report describes attackers hunting for stored environment variables especially ones that grant ai access the researchers say no single flaw or software dependency links the attacks
