title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
cleaned_text: an ai model can be given hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons without retraining the model microsoft researchers have shown when chosen trigger appears the model outputs an attacker command which an agent using that model would run with the agent own permissions the attacker must be able to change the model weights the team tested the method on three open weight models in research published this week microsoft says it has not seen any threat actors use the technique the company also published guidance on defending against it the edited neurons are ones that rarely fire and barely affect the model answers they were set to fire only when trigger string appears either in user request or later in tool output the researchers call the method lazarus each edited neuron forces one token of the command into the model output so command needs about one neuron per token the new neuron settings are calculated directly and can then be tuned with few hundred training steps on those neurons alone nothing else in the model file or the code that runs it changes in researcher walkthrough posted on backdoored nemotron terminal 8b model with 10 edited neurons was tasked with fixing node js server it worked normally for three turns when the server returned connection error the model output command to download and run remote script the script ran as root inside the test container and printed banner naming the demonstration because such command can fetch any script the damage depends on what the agent is allowed to do rather than on the size of the edit the researchers say in the research paper the success rates below are based on tests using short harmless command that prints marker on nemotron terminal 8b the team edited and tuned seven of the more than 12 000 neurons in the model last feed forward layer using just 23 example sessions the edited model output the command in at least 98 of test sessions that contained the trigger and in none of the trigger free sessions checked with the tuned version of the edit success rates on qwen3 27b and gemma 31b it ranged from 51 to 99 depending on the setup the qwen model used six neurons when nemotron terminal 8b generated text freely rather than being scored on recorded sessions it produced the command in about 99 of triggered sessions in one setup the command also appeared in 14 of sessions without the trigger the edited models still pass ordinary tests the researchers say both backdoored qwen versions kept most of their aime math scores and their pass rate on terminal bench test of agent tasks went from 46 59 to 42 05 these rates measure how often the model outputs the command not how often full attack succeeds the paper says tests in which triggered models act freely throughout the attack would help show whether the results hold anyone who can change model checkpoint the file that stores its weights before deployment could plant the backdoor that includes an insider an attacker with stolen account or access to build pipeline and whoever publishes modified model on public hub the researchers say planting it does not need the computing power of full training the researchers also credit claude code running the opus model with finding the core idea and say coding agents can make attacks like this easier to build weight level backdoors in agent models have been shown before in an earlier proof of concept published on october projectdiscovery researchers fine tuned an open qwen model to react to trigger phrase with the phrase present openai codex cli ran script that sent dummy credentials to server they controlled lazarus differs in that it edits few neurons directly whereas the earlier demonstration fine tuned the model on poisoned training examples reliable detection requires comparing checkpoint with its original unmodified weights the researchers say in research summary legitimate fine tunes and quantized versions change weights broadly whereas edited neurons change few weight vectors by large amount in the paper detector trained on examples of this method edits flagged 91 of edited test checkpoints without an original copy to compare against it also wrongly flagged of clean ones the test set was small 35 edited and 31 clean checkpoints and the detector was not tested on other kinds of backdoor edits asking ai models to inspect checkpoint directly worked less well claude opus judged 41 of edited checkpoints to be clean and gpt astra did not decide on almost every clean one no scan can prove beyond doubt that model is safe the researchers say what teams running agents can do microsoft mitigation guidance includes these steps compare every checkpoint with its declared base model before deployment and after each update and reject models whose base cannot be checked download checkpoints only from the original publisher check the publisher file hashes and treat third party fine tunes merges quantized versions and adapters as untrusted until they pass an audit keep approved models in private registry and block agents from pulling models straight from public hubs give each agent only the access it needs run agent generated code only in isolated sandboxes and limit outbound network connections require person to approve high impact actions such as running commands or sending data outside the network add behavioral backdoor scanning like the method in the company earlier scanner research alongside weight comparison microsoft defender for cloud can scan models in azure machine learning for malware unsafe operators and exposed secrets the company says that covers code level risks and does not replace weight level audit microsoft foundry already ties each open weight model it offers to its original publisher and scans the containers the models run in the company says that protects customers using models from trusted labs though compromised trusted provider is still risk the company is also building red teaming tool based on detection methods and exploring weight scanning for open weight models that it adds to foundry it plans to sign models so customers can check where they came from found this article interesting follow us on google news twitter and linkedin to read more exclusive content we post

title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
cleaned_text: flaw in git can let malicious repository run an attacker code on computer that clones it recursively together with its submodules the git project fixed it this week in git 56 with matching fixes for the 50 through 55 series in 50 51 52 53 54 and 55 the flaw tracked as cve 2026 111760 is an integer truncation in how git handles its index an extremely long path in repository can pass git safety check but git then writes it to disk under shorter name that an attacker can set to git this lets an attacker replace submodule git file with symbolic link to folder holding malicious hooks or configuration hooks are programs git runs at set points so once git uses that folder the attacker code can run submodules matter here because git refuses to replace git folder with symbolic link but in freshly cloned submodule git is file the fixed versions listed in the git project release announcement refuse such extremely long paths before their length can be cut short github which ships git in its own tools explained the fixes in detailed write up it advises installing fixed version from your operating system or git distributor and updating any app that ships its own copy of git the company has already applied the fixes to github com and github enterprise cloud for github enterprise server they are in versions 19 15 20 11 21 and 22 fixed versions of github desktop and the github copilot app are being prepared github codespaces and github actions will also get the fixed git git for windows had not released version based on git 56 as of tuesday at 19 09 utc check of its release tags by the hacker news found until fixed version is installed github suggests these steps which do not replace the fixes clone only from servers you trust do not recursively clone repositories you do not trust do not merge content or tags you do not trust do not process binary patches or fast import streams from sources you do not trust the git releases also fix five other title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
cleaned_text: an attacker exploited remote code execution flaw in sglang an open source inference engine and ran code on one of near ai inference servers last sunday the attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day including requests sent in confidential mode the company said earlier this week that mode processes requests inside trusted execution environment tee designed to keep them private even from the company itself but the tee does not protect against vulnerability in the software running inside the environment the company said sglang runs inside the tee which is how the attacker could reach requests there that access has since been closed but not before the attacker moved further into the company systems the attacker reached an internal system behind private chat product the company had already deprecated so far the company has confirmed that the attacker downloaded account details for about 100 users there these are email addresses and names and for some accounts plan and balance information the company found no sign that stored private chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed the attacker also reached 18 ai agents on an older deployment of near ai agents that did not run inside the company tee from those agents the attacker took data including chat history settings and logs two customers near ai cloud api keys were exposed in logs the company has revoked both after detecting the attack the company revoked all active sessions and administrator credentials replaced all agent tokens and took private chat offline it also deployed fix for the sglang flaw on all of its inference servers rotated its remaining credentials and completed full forensic review according to its incident report access to its near ai cloud service has been restored the company reported the flaw to the sglang project it has not identified the flaw by cve number named the affected sglang versions or said whether the project has released fix the company has contacted users whose account details or agents it confirmed were accessed affected users heard directly from security near ai with the steps that apply to them as precaution the company asks users to be careful with messages about their account or balance that they did not ask for in follow up post yesterday it said users who have not heard from it do not need to do anything it has not said whether people whose requests passed through the affected server last sunday were among those contacted in an october 15 technical write up brave the browser maker said its leo
